36.question_text_en:
Consider the following statements: Statement I: The
5th Five-year plan proposes the twin objectives of
removing poverty and attaining self-reliance. Statement II:
The rolling plan was launched between the sixth and the
seventh five-year plan, Which of the above statements
is/are correct?
36.question_text_hi:
Consider the following statements: Statement I: The
5th Five-year plan proposes the twin objectives of
removing poverty and attaining self-reliance. Statement II:
The rolling plan was launched between the sixth and the
seventh five-year plan, Which of the above statements
is/are correct?

options.text_en: Both statements I and II are correct
options.text_hi: Both statements I and II are correct

options.text_en: Both statements I and II are incorrect
options.text_hi: Both statements I and II are incorrect

options.text_en: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
options.text_hi: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect

options.text_en: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
options.text_hi: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct

36.explanation_en:
Statement I is correct because the Fifth Five-Year
Plan (1974–1979) focused explicitly on "Garibi
Hatao" (removal of poverty) and achieving self-re-
liance. Statement II is incorrect because the
Rolling Plan was introduced by the Janata Party gov-
ernment between the Fifth and Sixth Five-Year
Plans (1978–1980), not between the sixth and seventh.
Important Facts:
➤ The draft of the Fifth Five-Year Plan was pre-
pared and launched under the guidance of D.P. Dhar.
➤ The Fifth Plan introduced the landmark Minimum
Needs Programme (MNP) in 1974.
➤ The concept of the Rolling Plan was originally con-
ceptualized by Swedish economist Gunnar Myrdal.
➤ The Janata Party government terminated the Fifth
Plan a year early in 1978 and initiated the Rolling Plan
for 1978–1980.
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan was later formally im-
plemented for the period 1980–1985 under the
Congress government.

37.question_text_en:
What is the rationale behind granting Maharatna
status to certain Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)?
37.question_text_hi:
What is the rationale behind granting Maharatna
status to certain Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)?

options.text_en: To limit their autonomy in financial decisions
options.text_hi: To limit their autonomy in financial decisions

options.text_en: To provide greater financial and operational autonomy
options.text_hi: To provide greater financial and operational autonomy

options.text_en: To bring them under state government control
options.text_hi: To bring them under state government control

37.explanation_en:
The primary objective of conferring Maharatna sta-
tus on eligible Central Public Sector Enterprises
(CPSEs) is to empower mega-enterprises with greater
operational and financial autonomy, enabling
them to expand operations, make substantial capital in-
vestments, and emerge as global giants.
Important Facts:
➤ The Maharatna category for Central Public
Sector Enterprises was introduced by the Government of
India in May 2010.
➤ Maharatna CPSE boards can decide on equity in-
vestment in joint ventures/subsidiaries up to 15% of
net worth (or Rs5,000 crore) without prior government
approval.
➤ To qualify for Maharatna status, a CPSE must already
hold Navratna status and be listed on an Indian
stock exchange.
➤ The qualifying criteria include an average annual net
profit of over Rs5,000 crore and average annual
turnover of over Rs25,000 crore over the past three
years.
➤ Prominent Maharatna companies include ONGC,
NTPC, IOCL, SAIL, BHEL, and Coal India
Limited.

38.question_text_en:
Before 1991, a system of licenses, quotas, and
permits restricted private sector growth. What was this
system called?
38.question_text_hi:
Before 1991, a system of licenses, quotas, and
permits restricted private sector growth. What was this
system called?
38.explanation_en:
The elaborate bureaucratic framework of licenses, per-
mits, and quotas governing the establishment and ex-
pansion of private businesses in India prior to 1991 was
popularly termed the "License Raj" (or Permit Raj). It
was dismantled by the historic New Economic
Policy (NEP) of 1991.
Important Facts:
➤ The term "License Raj" was originally coined by vet-
eran freedom fighter and Swatantra Party founder C.
Rajagopalachari.
➤ Under this regime, the Industries (Development
and Regulation) Act, 1951 required firms to secure
government licenses to open, produce, or expand fac-
tory capacities.
➤ The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade
Practices (MRTP) Act, 1969 placed severe caps

on the growth and assets of large corporations.
➤ The historic 1991 economic reforms were intro-
duced under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and
Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
➤ The 1991 reforms ushered in the LPG model
(Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation), abolish-
ing industrial licensing for most sectors.

39.question_text_en:
Which Article provides for the establishment of an
Inter-State Council?
39.question_text_hi:
Which Article provides for the establishment of an
Inter-State Council?
39.explanation_en:
Article 263 of the Constitution of India provides for the
establishment of an Inter-State Council by the
President of India to investigate and discuss subjects of
common interest between the Union and the States or
among the States themselves.
Important Facts:
➤ The Inter-State Council was formally established in
1990 by a Presidential Order on the recommendation of
the Sarkaria Commission (1983–1988).
➤ The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-of-
ficio Chairman of the Inter-State Council.
➤ The members include Chief Ministers of all States,
Chief Ministers of UTs with legislative assemblies,
Administrators of other UTs, and six Union Cabinet
Ministers.
➤ The Council functions as an advisory body to foster
cooperative federalism and resolve inter-governmental
disputes.
➤ Article 262 separately deals with the adjudication
of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers or river
valleys.

40.question_text_en:
How many types of emergencies can be proclaimed
by the President of India under the Constitution?
40.question_text_hi:
How many types of emergencies can be proclaimed
by the President of India under the Constitution?
40.explanation_en:
Part XVIII of the Constitution of India provides for three
types of emergencies that can be proclaimed by
the President: National Emergency (Article 352),
State Emergency / President's Rule (Article 356),
and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
Important Facts:

➤ National Emergency (Article 352) is invoked
on the grounds of war, external aggression, or armed re-
bellion.
➤ The phrase "armed rebellion" replaced "internal dis-
turbance" via the 44th Constitutional Amendment
Act, 1978.
➤ President's Rule (Article 356) is declared upon
the failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
➤ Financial Emergency (Article 360) can be de-
clared if the financial stability or credit of India is threat-
ened; it has never been proclaimed in India.
➤ Emergency provisions in the Indian Constitution are
borrowed primarily from the Government of India
Act, 1935, while suspension of Fundamental Rights
during emergency is drawn from the Weimar
Constitution of Germany.

41.question_text_en:
In a federal system resting on "limited government,"
the Supreme Court is designed to be the final authority for
what specific purpose?
41.question_text_hi:
In a federal system resting on "limited government,"
the Supreme Court is designed to be the final authority for
what specific purpose?
41.explanation_en:
In a constitutional federal democracy governed by the
principle of limited government, the Supreme Court func-

tions as the final arbiter and authoritative inter-
preter of the Constitution. This safeguards federal
equilibrium and prevents organs of state from encroach-
ing beyond their prescribed constitutional jurisdictions.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Article 132 and Article 133, the Supreme
Court of India exercises appellate jurisdiction over sub-
stantial questions of constitutional interpretation.
➤ The concept of Judicial Review empowers the
Supreme Court to invalidate legislative or executive acts
violating the Constitution (Article 13).
➤ Article 141 mandates that the law declared by the
Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the
territory of India.
➤ The doctrine of Basic Structure was propounded
by the Supreme Court in the landmark Kesavananda
Bharati case (1973).
➤ Under Article 32, the Supreme Court is designated
as the guarantor and protector of Fundamental Rights.

42.question_text_en:
Which of the following is newly introduced in Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhita?
42.question_text_hi:
Which of the following is newly introduced in Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhita?

options.text_en: Mob lynching as a specific offence
options.text_hi: Mob lynching as a specific offence

42.explanation_en:
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has codified
mob lynching as a distinct and separate penal of-
fence under Section 103(2). Under this provision, murder
committed by a mob of five or more persons on grounds
of race, caste, sex, place of birth, language, or personal
belief attracts capital punishment or life imprisonment.
Important Facts:
➤ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 re-
placed the Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
➤ Section 103(2) of the BNS specifically prescribes
punishment for murder committed by five or more per-
sons acting in concert.
➤ The prescribed punishment for mob lynching ranges
from life imprisonment to the death penalty,
along with a fine.
➤ The new criminal laws, including BNS, BNSS, and
BSA, came into official force across India on 1 July
2024.
➤ Sedition was omitted and replaced by offences en-
dangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of
India under Section 152.

43.question_text_en: Which is the brightest star visible in the night sky?
43.question_text_hi: Which is the brightest star visible in the night sky?
43.explanation_en:
Sirius, commonly known as the Dog Star, is the
brightest individual star visible in Earth's night sky, with
an apparent visual magnitude of −1.46. It is located in
the constellation Canis Major.

Important Facts:
➤ Sirius appears remarkably bright primarily because of
its intrinsic luminosity combined with its proximity to
Earth (about 8.6 light-years away).
➤ Sirius is actually a binary star system consisting of a
main-sequence star (Sirius A) and a faint white dwarf
companion (Sirius B).
➤ The second brightest star visible in the night sky is
Canopus, situated in the constellation Carina with an
apparent magnitude of −0.74.
➤ Polaris (the North Star) is an indicator of celestial
north, but ranks only around the 48th brightest star in the
night sky.
➤ Alpha Centauri is the closest star system to our
Solar System, located at approximately 4.37 light-
years.

44.question_text_en:
According to Hugo de Vries, what is the primary cause
of speciation?
44.question_text_hi:
According to Hugo de Vries, what is the primary cause
of speciation?
44.explanation_en:
Dutch botanist Hugo de Vries proposed the
Mutation Theory of Evolution, asserting that spe-
ciation is caused by sudden, discontinuous large mu-
tations rather than the gradual minor variations pro-
posed by Charles Darwin. He termed this single-step
large mutation causing speciation as saltation.
Important Facts:
➤ Hugo de Vries formulated his Mutation Theory based
on his breeding experiments with the evening primrose
plant (Oenothera lamarckiana).
➤ Unlike Darwinian variations which are small and di-
rectional, mutations according to De Vries are random
and directionless.
➤ De Vries coined the term "saltation", meaning a
single-step, drastic mutation leading to the emergence of
a new species.
➤ Hugo de Vries is also celebrated as one of the three
scientists who independently rediscovered Gregor
Mendel's laws of inheritance in 1900.
➤ Modern evolutionary synthesis subsequently inte-
grated both Darwinian natural selection and genetic
mutations.

Dutch botanist Hugo de Vries proposed the
Mutation Theory of Evolution, asserting that spe-
ciation is caused by sudden, discontinuous large mu-
tations rather than the gradual minor variations pro-
posed by Charles Darwin. He termed this single-step
large mutation causing speciation as saltation.
Important Facts:
➤ Hugo de Vries formulated his Mutation Theory based
on his breeding experiments with the evening primrose
plant (Oenothera lamarckiana).
➤ Unlike Darwinian variations which are small and di-
rectional, mutations according to De Vries are random
and directionless.
➤ De Vries coined the term "saltation", meaning a
single-step, drastic mutation leading to the emergence of
a new species.
➤ Hugo de Vries is also celebrated as one of the three
scientists who independently rediscovered Gregor
Mendel's laws of inheritance in 1900.
➤ Modern evolutionary synthesis subsequently inte-
grated both Darwinian natural selection and genetic
mutations.

45.explanation_en:
The primary scientific objective of the Major
Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE)
telescope at Hanle, Ladakh is the detection and ob-
servation of high-energy cosmic gamma rays. It
studies astrophysical phenomena such as blazars, pul-
sars, and supernova remnants through atmospheric
Cherenkov radiation.
Important Facts:
➤ The MACE telescope was constructed by the
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) with
technical support from ECIL and other Indian partners.
➤ Positioned at an altitude of approximately 4,300
metres, MACE is the highest Cherenkov telescope in
the world.
➤ With a diameter of 21 metres, it is the second-
largest atmospheric Cherenkov telescope in the world.
➤ Hanle is situated in the Cold Desert of Ladakh,
recognized as a designated Dark Sky Reserve due
to pristine cloudless skies.
➤ The observatory detects Cherenkov flashes produced
when incoming very-high-energy (VHE) gamma
rays interact with Earth's upper atmosphere.

parks, while Assam has 7.

National Park.

Reintroduction Project launched in 2022.
➤ Madhya Pradesh also holds the highest tiger popula-
tion in the country, earning the moniker "Tiger State
of India".
➤ India's very first national park was Hailey National
Park (presently Jim Corbett National Park), es-
tablished in 1936 in Uttarakhand.
➤ Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest na-
tional park in India by area, spanning over 4,400 sq
km.

47.explanation_en:
Han Kang's celebrated novel "We Do Not Part" re-

human life."

first Asian woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
➤ She previously achieved global prominence when her
novel "The Vegetarian" won the International
Booker Prize in 2016 (translated by Deborah Smith).
➤ The original Korean edition of *We Do Not Part* was
published in 2021 under the title *Jakbyeolhaji anne-
unda*.
➤ Her other internationally acclaimed novels include
"Human Acts" (2014) and "The White Book"
(2016).

framework?

options.text_en: Knowledge Drivers and Innovation Impact Index

options.text_hi: Innovation Input and Innovation Output Sub-Indices

49.explanation_en:
The Global Innovation Index (GII) framework is
structured around two primary pillars: the Innovation
Input Sub-Index and the Innovation Output Sub-
Index. Together, these sub-indices measure the en-
abling environment for innovation and the actual results
achieved.
Important Facts:
➤ The GII is published annually by the World
Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a
specialized agency of the United Nations.
➤ The Innovation Input Sub-Index evaluates five
pillars: Institutions, Human capital & research,
Infrastructure, Market sophistication, and Business so-
phistication.
➤ The Innovation Output Sub-Index evaluates
two pillars: Knowledge & technology outputs and
Creative outputs.
➤ The overall GII score is calculated as the average of
the Input and Output sub-indices.
➤ India has witnessed significant progress in the GII
rankings over the past decade, entering the top 40 in-
novative economies globally.

50.question_text_en:
Which initiative was launched in 2025 to provide
digital identities and simplify verification for Indian Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)?
50.question_text_hi:
Which initiative was launched in 2025 to provide
digital identities and simplify verification for Indian Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)?
50.explanation_en:
The Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) was instituted
by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
(MSME) to bring informal micro-enterprises into the for-
mal economic net by generating a formal digital iden-
tifier (Udyam Assist Certificate). This enables
small business units to seamlessly access priority sector
lending and statutory benefits.
Important Facts:
➤ The UAP initiative was developed by the Small
Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
as the nodal implementing agency.
➤ It targets non-GST registered informal micro enter-
prises (IMEs) to facilitate access to Priority Sector
Lending (PSL).
➤ Formal registration on the main Udyam Portal origi-
nally commenced on 1 July 2020 following revised
MSME definitions.
➤ The revised MSME definition incorporates composite
criteria of investment in plant/machinery and an-
nual turnover.
➤ For a Micro Enterprise, the ceiling is set at invest-
ment up to Rs1 crore and turnover up to Rs5 crore.

it. The "now" is always pregnant with the "next".
Were we to experience a moment in total isolation,
stripped of all context and memory, it (C) to have any
human meaning. It would be a "flash" without a narrative,
a sensation without a self. Our very identity is built upon
the temporal continuity that phenomenology seeks to
describe and analyse.
While objective clocks measure seconds with mechanical
precision, the "lived time" of the individual is notoriously
elastic. An hour spent in a state of flow can feel like
minutes, while a minute of intense physical pain can feel
like an eternity. The clock is a social (D) ; the experience
of duration is a biological and psychological reality.
This subjective stretching of duration is what makes a
moment of joy feel fleeting and a moment of dread feel
interminable. We are not mere observers of time; we are
the medium (E) which time gains its quality. To understand
the human condition, we must look beyond the stopwatch
and into the shifting currents of internal experience.
Choose the correct adverb to begin the sentence: (A)

Fill in the blank: The World Trade Organisation (WTO)
was founded in the year ________ as the successor to

28.explanation_en:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) officially
commenced operations on 1 January 1995 under the
Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the General
Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) that
had been in place since 1948.
Important Facts:
➤ The WTO was created following negotiations con-
cluding the Uruguay Round (1986–1994).
➤ The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is
situated in Geneva, Switzerland.
➤ Unlike GATT, which covered only trade in goods, the
WTO encompasses trade in services (GATS) and intel-
lectual property (TRIPS).
➤ As of recent accessions, the WTO comprises 166
member nations.
➤ Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first woman
and the first African to serve as Director-General of the
WTO.

29.question_text_en:
In the context of the Gupta administration, what did
the term 'Uparika' signify?
29.question_text_hi:
In the context of the Gupta administration, what did
the term 'Uparika' signify?
29.explanation_en:
During the Gupta period, the empire was divided into
provinces known as Bhuktis, and the administrative
head or governor appointed over a Bhukti was desig-
nated as Uparika (or *Uparika Maharaja*).
Important Facts:
➤ Provinces (*Bhuktis*) were further subdivided into
districts termed Vishayas, administered by a
Vishayapati.
➤ The *Vishayapati* was assisted in district administra-
tion by an advisory council including the *Nagara
Sreshthi*, *Sarthavaha*, *Prathama Kulika*, and
*Prathama Kayastha*.
➤ Village level administration was managed by the vil-
lage headman called Gramika or *Gramadhyaksha*.
➤ Military commanders were designated as
Mahabaladhikrita or *Senapati*.
➤ The Gupta empire represented a decentralized ad-
ministrative structure with considerable local autonomy
given to provincial rulers.

30.explanation_en:
Ibn Battuta's uncritical, casual accounts of purchasing,
employing, and presenting enslaved men and women as
customary gifts reflect the historical reality that slavery
was a deeply institutionalized, ubiquitous,
and socially normalized practice across the me-
dieval Islamic world and medieval Indian society.
Important Facts:
➤ Ibn Battuta was a renowned 14th-century
Moroccan scholar and traveler who arrived in India in
1333 during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin
Tughlaq.
➤ He documented his travels across Africa, Asia, and
India in his famous book 'Rihla' (written in Arabic).
➤ Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta as the Qazi (judge)
of Delhi, a post he held for several years.
➤ In his writings, he records purchasing slaves, horses,
and almonds as customary presents to offer to the
Sultan.
➤ Female slaves were widely employed in imperial
households for domestic service, music, and royal
espionage.

31.explanation_en:
François Bernier observed that despite widespread op-
pression of artisans and absence of private property
rights under Mughal rule, Indian textiles and handicrafts
dominated international commerce, bringing immense in-
flows of gold and silver. This apparent paradox demon-
strates that under specific historical and structural condi-
tions, a narrative of domestic artisanal dis-
tress can coexist with flourishing external
trade.
Important Facts:
➤ François Bernier was a French physician and
traveler who visited India during the reign of Emperor
Aurangzeb (1656–1668).
➤ He authored the famous travelogue 'Travels in the
Mogul Empire'.
➤ Bernier argued that the absence of private land own-
ership in the Mughal Empire was the primary cause of its
economic degradation.
➤ He described Mughal India as a place where the king

33.question_text_en: Microeconomics primarily deals with:
33.question_text_hi: Microeconomics primarily deals with:
33.explanation_en:
Microeconomics is the branch of economics that fo-
cuses on the behavior, decision-making, and resource
allocation of individual economic units, such as
single consumers, households, and individual business
firms.
Important Facts:
➤ The terms 'microeconomics' and 'macroeconomics'
were coined by Norwegian economist Ragnar Frisch
in 1933.
➤ Key theories under microeconomics include con-
sumer demand theory, theory of the firm, and market
equilibrium pricing.
➤ In contrast, macroeconomics examines aggre-
gate economic phenomena such as national income,
gross domestic product, inflation, and fiscal budgets.
➤ Microeconomic analysis relies heavily on the ce-
teris paribus (all other things being equal) assump-
tion.
➤ The interaction of supply and demand in individual
product and factor markets is central to microeconomic
study.

34.question_text_en: A good with negative income elasticity is called:
34.question_text_hi: A good with negative income elasticity is called:
34.explanation_en:
An inferior good is defined as a commodity whose de-
mand decreases when consumer income increases, giv-
ing it a negative income elasticity of demand
($E_y < 0$).
Important Facts:
➤ Income elasticity of demand measures the
percentage change in quantity demanded in response to
a percentage change in consumer income.
➤ A normal good has a positive income elasticity of
demand ($E_y > 0$), meaning consumption rises as in-
come increases.
➤ A luxury good is a category of normal goods where
income elasticity is greater than one ($E_y > 1$).
➤ A Giffen good is a special sub-category of inferior
goods where the quantity demanded increases as price
increases, violating the Law of Demand.
➤ Examples of inferior goods include low-grade cereals
or basic public transport services that people substitute
as they become wealthier.

During the terminal year of the Sixth Five-Year Plan

severe drought and famine-like conditions due to
deficient and erratic monsoon rainfall, which adversely
affected agricultural productivity and rural food grain
supplies.

1985 under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira
Gandhi.

while the achieved growth rate was 5.7%.
➤ The Sixth Plan marked the beginning of economic lib-
eralization and shifted emphasis towards poverty allevia-
tion.
➤ Major anti-poverty programmes like the Integrated
Rural Development Programme (IRDP) and
NREP were expanded during this plan.
➤ The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural
Development (NABARD) was established during
this period on 12 July 1982.

36.question_text_en:
What is mob lynching under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS)?
36.question_text_hi:
What is mob lynching under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS)?

options.text_en:
Involves violence by a group on grounds like identity or
suspicion
options.text_hi:
Involves violence by a group on grounds like identity or
suspicion

options.text_en: Applies only when religious motives are proven
options.text_hi: Applies only when religious motives are proven

options.text_en: Requires prior conspiracy among all members
options.text_hi: Requires prior conspiracy among all members

options.text_en: It is treated as simple assault
options.text_hi: It is treated as simple assault

36.explanation_en:
Under Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita (BNS), 2023, mob lynching is specifically
defined as an offence where a group of five or more per-
sons acting in concert commits murder on grounds of
race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language,
personal belief or any other similar ground.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Section 103(2) of the BNS, the penalty for
mob lynching ranges from life imprisonment to capital
punishment (death penalty), alongside a fine.
➤ The provision does not restrict motive to religion
alone; it broadly covers caste, race, linguistic identity, or
similar characteristics.
➤ The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the
colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
➤ The new criminal laws officially came into effect
across India on 1 July 2024.
➤ Prior to the BNS, the IPC had no separate, dedicated
statutory penal provision specifically penalizing mob
lynching.

37.question_text_en:
What is the distinction between terrorism and
organized crime?
37.question_text_hi:
What is the distinction between terrorism and
organized crime?

options.text_en:
There is no distinction under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS).
options.text_hi:
There is no distinction under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS).

options.text_en:
Terrorism aims to threaten national security, while organized
crime focuses on unlawful gain.

Terrorism aims to threaten national security, while organized
crime focuses on unlawful gain.

options.text_en: Organized crime is limited to violent offences only.
options.text_hi: Organized crime is limited to violent offences only.

37.explanation_en:
In legal and criminological frameworks, including the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), terrorist acts are
motivated by ideological, political, or subversive goals
aimed at threatening the sovereignty, unity, and security
of the nation or terrorizing the public, whereas orga-
nized crime is driven by continuous unlawful activity
for material or financial benefit.
Important Facts:
➤ Under the BNS, terrorist acts are defined and pe-
nalized under Section 113.
➤ Organized crime is explicitly defined and penal-
ized as a distinct offence under Section 111 of the
BNS.
➤ Organized crime syndicates engage in illicit activities
like extortion, kidnapping, drug trafficking, and cyber-
crimes primarily for economic profit.
➤ Terrorism utilizes calculated acts of violence, sabo-
tage, and fear to destabilize government authority or
public safety.
➤ While organized crime syndicates and terror groups
occasionally form operational nexus, their core motiva-
tional objectives remain distinct.

38.question_text_en: The crust is described as brittle in nature because:
38.question_text_hi: The crust is described as brittle in nature because:

options.text_en: It is composed of soft minerals
options.text_hi: It is composed of soft minerals

38.explanation_en:
The Earth's crust is described as brittle because it is
cold, rigid, and solid; when subjected to tectonic forces,
differential stress, and strain exceeding its elastic limit, it
fractures and breaks rather than undergoing ductile de-
formation.
Important Facts:
➤ The crust is the outermost solid shell of the Earth,
categorized into continental and oceanic crust.
➤ The continental crust is thicker and largely granitic
(Sial), while the oceanic crust is denser and basaltic
(Sima).
➤ Sudden fractures and displacements along faults in
the brittle crust cause earthquakes.
➤ Below the crust lies the Mohorovicic discontinu-
ity (Moho), which separates the crust from the mantle.
➤ Deeper mantle rocks deform plastically due to im-
mense temperature and confining pressure, contrasting
with the brittle crust.

39.question_text_en:
The North Western mineral region of India is
composed of territories from which of the following pairs of
states?
39.question_text_hi:
The North Western mineral region of India is
composed of territories from which of the following pairs of
states?
39.explanation_en:
The North-Western mineral belt of India covers
the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and extends into parts
of Gujarat. This region is rich in non-ferrous metallic
minerals, building stones, salt, and petroleum reserves.
Important Facts:
➤ Rajasthan is well known for rich deposits of copper,
lead, zinc, gypsum, marble, and sandstone.
➤ Gujarat is noted for petroleum and natural gas re-
serves (Ankleshwar, Cambay basin), salt production,
and bauxite.
➤ The famous Khetri Copper Belt and Zawar
zinc-lead mines are situated in Rajasthan within this
belt.
➤ Sedimentary rocks in this region are rich in non-
metallic mineral deposits such as limestone and fuller's
earth.
➤ This region contrasts with the Chota Nagpur plateau,
which is India's mineral heartland dominated by iron ore
and coal.

40.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: The largest linguistic group in India
belongs to the ________ language family.
40.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: The largest linguistic group in India
belongs to the ________ language family.
40.explanation_en:
The Indo-Aryan sub-family of the Indo-European lan-
guage family constitutes the largest linguistic group in
India, spoken by approximately 78% of the country's
population. It includes prominent languages such as
Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi, and Gujarati.
Important Facts:
➤ The second-largest linguistic family in India is the
Dravidian family, spoken by about 20% of the popula-
tion.
➤ The Austro-Asiatic (Austric) family is spoken by
around 1.11% of the population, including languages
like Santhali and Khasi.
➤ The Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) family ac-
counts for roughly 0.85% of the population, predomi-
nantly in the Northeastern states.
➤ The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
currently recognizes 22 official languages.
➤ Hindi, Bengali, and Marathi are the three most spo-
ken native languages in India as per Census data.

41.question_text_en:
Which of the following best explains the role of
enzymes in biochemical reactions?
41.question_text_hi:
Which of the following best explains the role of
enzymes in biochemical reactions?

options.text_en: They act as catalysts lowering activation energy
options.text_hi: They act as catalysts lowering activation energy

options.text_en: They change the end products permanently
options.text_hi: They change the end products permanently

41.explanation_en:
Enzymes act as biological catalysts that accelerate
chemical reactions by lowering the activation en-
ergy required for the transformation of substrates into
products, without being consumed or permanently al-
tered in the process.
Important Facts:
➤ Almost all enzymes are globular proteins, with the
exception of certain catalytic RNA molecules known as
ribozymes.
➤ The specific region of the enzyme where substrate
molecules bind and undergo reaction is called the ac-
tive site.
➤ The lock-and-key model was proposed by Emil
Fischer, while Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-
fit model.
➤ Enzymes do not alter the chemical equilibrium of a
reversible reaction; they merely accelerate the rate of
reaching equilibrium.
➤ Optimum enzyme catalytic activity is dependent on
physiological temperature and pH conditions.

43.question_text_en:
What is the world-leading resolution of the Bharat
Forecasting System?
43.question_text_hi:
What is the world-leading resolution of the Bharat
Forecasting System?
43.explanation_en:
The Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS), de-
veloped by the Pune-based Indian Institute of Tropical
Meteorology (IITM) and deployed by the India
Meteorological Department (IMD), delivers numerical
weather prediction at a global benchmark 6-kilometer
resolution.
Important Facts:
➤ The system significantly improves localized weather
forecasts, extreme rainfall warnings, and cyclone track
predictions.
➤ It was adopted to replace earlier global forecasting
models operating at a 12-kilometer grid resolution.
➤ It utilizes the state-of-the-art high-performance super-
computing systems Arka and Arunika.
➤ The model is developed under the aegis of the
Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
➤ The high spatial resolution enables accurate pin-
pointing of micro-climatic and small-scale thunderstorm
events.

44.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: The IMEC initiative aims to
strengthen connectivity between India and ________
region.
44.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: The IMEC initiative aims to
strengthen connectivity between India and ________
region.
44.explanation_en:
The India-Middle East-Europe Economic
Corridor (IMEC) was announced during the 2023
G20 New Delhi Summit to stimulate economic de-
velopment by fostering connectivity between India, the
Arabian Gulf (Middle East), and Europe. It com-
prises two distinct corridors: the East Corridor connect-
ing India to the Arabian Gulf and the Northern Corridor
connecting the Arabian Gulf to Europe.
Important Facts:
➤ IMEC was launched on 9 September 2023 on
the sidelines of the G20 Summit in New Delhi.
➤ The project includes railway networks, ship-to-rail
transit networks, and road transport routes.
➤ Key signatories include India, the US, the UAE,
Saudi Arabia, France, Germany, Italy, and the
EU.
➤ Along with transport routes, it aims to deploy electric-
ity cables, high-speed digital lines, and clean hydrogen
pipelines.
➤ It is positioned as an alternative connectivity and
trade network to China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).

incentivize which type of actions?

based mechanism designed to incentivize voluntary en-
vironmentally positive actions undertaken by in-
dividuals, communities, and private industries, thereby
promoting sustainable living and ecological restoration.

➤ The programme was officially launched by the Prime
Minister during the COP28 Summit in Dubai in 2023.
➤ It operates under the broader vision of the LiFE
(Lifestyle for Environment) movement.
➤ Key eligible activities include afforestation, water har-
vesting, sustainable agriculture, and waste manage-
ment.
➤ The Indian Council of Forestry Research
and Education (ICFRE) serves as the GCP adminis-
trator.
➤ Green credits generated are tradeable on a domestic
platform and are independent of standard carbon credits.

Right option (C): Columns I, II and IV
Explanation
Let Column I = x (2, 4, 6, 8, 10):
• Column II = x² + 2 → 2²+2 = 6, 4²+2 = 18, 6²+2 = 38,
8²+2 = 66, 10²+2 = 102.
• Column IV = x(x − 1) → 2×1 = 2, 4×3 = 12, 6×5 = 30,
8×7 = 56, 10×9 = 90.
Also, Column II = Column IV + Column I + 2.
Hence, Columns I, II and IV are connected with each
other.
✔ Answer: (C)

26.question_text_hi:

the following sports?
26.explanation_en:
En Passant (French for "in passing") is a special
pawn-capturing move in the game of Chess.
Important Facts:
➤ It allows a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn that
has moved forward two squares on its initial move as if it
had only advanced one square.
➤ The capturing pawn must be on its fifth rank (for
White) or fourth rank (for Black) to execute En Passant.
➤ The capture must be made on the very next turn im-
mediately following the opponent's double-step advance;
otherwise, the right is lost.
➤ Other special moves in chess include castling
(kingside and queenside) and pawn promotion.
➤ The governing international body for chess is the
International Chess Federation (FIDE), head-
quartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

27.question_text_en:
Which term refers to a situation in Chess where a
player is NOT in check but has no legal move available?
27.question_text_hi:
Which term refers to a situation in Chess where a
player is NOT in check but has no legal move available?
27.explanation_en:
In chess, a Stalemate occurs when the player whose
turn it is to move is not under check and has no legal
moves left, immediately resulting in a draw.
Important Facts:
➤ Under official FIDE rules, a stalemate immediately
ends the game with a half-point awarded to each player
(½–½).
➤ Checkmate, by contrast, occurs when a king is in
check and has no legal move to escape, ending the
game as a decisive loss.
➤ Stalemate is often utilized as a drawing tactic by a
player in an otherwise losing material position.
➤ Other drawing conditions in chess include threefold
repetition, fifty-move rule, and insufficient material.
➤ A standard chess game is played on an $8 \times 8$
grid consisting of 64 squares.

29.question_text_en:
Who authored the book 'Gulamgiri', a work that
exposed caste oppression and advocated social reform in
India?
29.question_text_hi:
Who authored the book 'Gulamgiri', a work that
exposed caste oppression and advocated social reform in
India?
29.explanation_en:
Jyotirao Govindrao Phule wrote the seminal book
'Gulamgiri' (Slavery) in 1873, critiquing the caste sys-
tem and dedicated to the American movement to abolish
slavery.
Important Facts:
➤ Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj
(Truth-Seekers' Society) in 1873 in Pune.
➤ He dedicated *Gulamgiri* to the good people of the
United States for their efforts in abolishing Black slavery.
➤ Along with his wife Savitribai Phule, he opened
the first school for girls at Bhide Wada in Pune in
1848.
➤ He was bestowed with the title 'Mahatma' in 1888
by social reformer Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar.
➤ His other prominent literary works include *Tritiya
Ratna*, *Brahmananche Kasab*, and *Shetkaryacha
Asud*.

31.question_text_en:
Which of the following rulers were responsible for the
extension of Saka power in western India?
31.question_text_hi:
Which of the following rulers were responsible for the
extension of Saka power in western India?
31.explanation_en:
Bhumaka and Nahapana were the prominent early
rulers of the Kshaharata dynasty of Western
Satraps (Sakas) who consolidated Saka authority across
western India.
Important Facts:
➤ Bhumaka was the earliest known Kshaharata ruler
whose coins have been found in Gujarat, Kathiawar, and
Malwa.
➤ Nahapana expanded the kingdom extensively into
parts of modern Maharashtra, Gujarat, and southern

Rajasthan.
➤ Nahapana assumed royal titles such as Rajan and
Kshatrapa on his bilingual coinages.
➤ The power of Nahapana was ultimately checked and
crushed by the Satavahana ruler Gautamiputra
Satakarni, as evidenced by the Jogalthambi
hoard of coins.
➤ The Western Satraps were divided into two main
branches: the Kshaharatas and the Kardamakas.

32.question_text_hi:
Which Maratha official was in charge of royal
correspondence, responsible for managing the Royal
Household and maintaining the daily court diary?
32.explanation_en:
In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan council of ministers, the
Sachiv (also known as *Shurnis*) oversaw royal corre-
spondence, checked official letters, and supervised royal
accounts and court records.
Important Facts:
➤ The Ashtapradhan was an advisory council of
eight ministers instituted by Chhatrapati Shivaji
Maharaj in 1674.
➤ The head of the council was the Peshwa (Prime
Minister), responsible for general administration.
➤ The Amatya (or *Majumdar*) was in charge of pub-
lic finance and maintained the accounts of the kingdom.
➤ The Sumant (or *Dabir*) functioned as the foreign
minister handling external affairs.
➤ The Danadhyaksha (or *Panditrao*) managed reli-
gious endowments and judicial ecclesiastical matters.

tual circle of his order.

35.question_text_en:
Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabilizer by
maintaining a fixed percentage of income?
35.question_text_hi:
Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabilizer by
maintaining a fixed percentage of income?
35.explanation_en:
A Proportional tax imposes the same constant tax
rate on all levels of income, automatically scaling tax col-
lection directly in proportion to total income changes.
Important Facts:
➤ Under a proportional tax system, the marginal tax
rate equals the average tax rate across all income brack-
ets.
➤ It is commonly referred to as a flat tax system.
➤ An automatic stabilizer moderates economic fluctua-
tions automatically without requiring fresh legislative in-
tervention.
➤ In contrast, a progressive tax takes a higher percent-
age from higher-income earners, whereas a regressive
tax imposes a heavier relative burden on low earners.
➤ Corporate income taxes with a single statutory rate
function essentially on a proportional structure.

36.question_text_en:
Which policy tool directly influences aggregate
demand through government spending?
36.question_text_hi:
Which policy tool directly influences aggregate
demand through government spending?
36.explanation_en:
Fiscal policy directly impacts aggregate demand in an
economy through adjustments in government ex-
penditure and taxation measures.
Important Facts:
➤ Fiscal policy is formulated and implemented by the
Ministry of Finance / Government.
➤ Aggregate demand comprises consumption ($C$), in-
vestment ($I$), government spending ($G$), and net ex-
ports ($X - M$).
➤ Monetary policy, by contrast, controls money sup-
ply and interest rates and is managed by the central
bank (Reserve Bank of India).
➤ Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing public
expenditure or lowering taxes to stimulate economic
growth.
➤ The theoretical foundation of fiscal intervention to
manage aggregate demand was established by John
Maynard Keynes.

______
37.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: The three main components of the
New Economic Policy are Liberalisation, Privatisation, and
______

mously structured around the three pillars of
Liberalisation, Privatisation, and
Globalisation (LPG).
Important Facts:

Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister
Dr. Manmohan Singh.

raj and dismantling unnecessary industrial restrictions.
➤ Privatisation encouraged private sector participa-
tion and strategic disinvestment in public sector enter-
prises.
➤ Globalisation opened the domestic economy to
foreign direct investments (FDI) and international trade
integration.
➤ The immediate catalyst for these sweeping reforms
was a severe Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis in
1991.

38.question_text_en:
The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is
applicable to which of the following?
38.question_text_hi:
The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is
applicable to which of the following?

options.text_en: Restricted only to civil court proceedings
options.text_hi: Restricted only to civil court proceedings

options.text_en: All judicial proceedings and all executive inquiries
options.text_hi: All judicial proceedings and all executive inquiries

options.text_en: Restricted only to High and Supreme Courts
options.text_hi: Restricted only to High and Supreme Courts

38.explanation_en:
Under Section 1, the Bharatiya Sakshya
Adhiniyam, 2023 applies to all judicial proceed-
ings in or before any court, including courts-martial
(other than those convened under specific service acts).
Important Facts:
➤ The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 replaced
the colonial Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
➤ The Act came into statutory force across India on 1
July 2024.
➤ It does not apply to affidavits presented to any court
or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator.
➤ It accords primary evidentiary status to electronic
and digital records, treating them on par with physi-
cal documents.
➤ The enactment forms part of the triad of new criminal
laws alongside the BNS, 2023 and the BNSS, 2023.

39.question_text_en:
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023, what is the defining feature of a "Zero FIR"?
39.question_text_hi:
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023, what is the defining feature of a "Zero FIR"?

options.text_en: A report where no specific suspect is named
options.text_hi: A report where no specific suspect is named

options.text_en: A report filed regardless of the crime's jurisdiction
options.text_hi: A report filed regardless of the crime's jurisdiction

options.text_en: A report filed electronically without visiting a station
options.text_hi: A report filed electronically without visiting a station

options.text_en: A report filed when no physical evidence exists
options.text_hi: A report filed when no physical evidence exists

39.explanation_en:
A Zero FIR allows a cognizable offence to be regis-
tered at any police station, irrespective of whether
the crime took place within its territorial jurisdiction.
Important Facts:
➤ Provision for Zero FIR is explicitly codified under
Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
➤ After recording the Zero FIR, the police station trans-
fers the case documents to the appropriate jurisdictional
police station for investigation.
➤ It ensures prompt registration of serious offences, es-
pecially crimes against women, without procedural de-
lays over jurisdiction.
➤ The concept gained legal momentum following the
recommendations of the Justice J.S. Verma
Committee in 2013.
➤ A Zero FIR is given the number serial 0 until it
reaches the concerned police station where a regular
FIR number is assigned.

40.question_text_en:
The outer core of the Earth's interior exists in which
physical state?
40.question_text_hi:
The outer core of the Earth's interior exists in which
physical state?
40.explanation_en:
The Earth's outer core exists in a liquid state due
to high temperatures exceeding the melting point of its
iron-nickel alloy.
Important Facts:
➤ The outer core extends from a depth of approxi-
mately 2,900 km to 5,150 km beneath the Earth's
surface.
➤ The boundary between the mantle and the outer core
is called the Gutenberg discontinuity.
➤ It is primarily composed of molten iron and nickel
(often termed the NiFe layer).
➤ Convection currents of molten iron in the outer core
generate the Earth's geomagnetic field via the geo-
dynamo effect.
➤
S-waves (secondary/shear seismic waves)
cannot pass through liquids and thus create an S-wave
shadow zone across the outer core.

cated in Kolkata, West Bengal.

Research Institute, one of the oldest tea research
centers in the world.

42.question_text_en:
Which of the following correctly describes the
components and charges involved in the formation of a
nucleosome?
42.question_text_hi:
Which of the following correctly describes the
components and charges involved in the formation of a
nucleosome?

options.text_en:
Negatively charged RNA wrapped around a neutral histone
octamer.
options.text_hi:
Negatively charged RNA wrapped around a neutral histone
octamer.

options.text_en:
Positively charged DNA wrapped around a negatively
charged histone hexamer.
options.text_hi:
Positively charged DNA wrapped around a negatively
charged histone hexamer.

options.text_en:
Negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively
charged histone octamer.
options.text_hi:
Negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively
charged histone octamer.

options.text_en:
Neutral DNA wrapped around a basic protein complex rich
in Lysine and Arginine.
options.text_hi:
Neutral DNA wrapped around a basic protein complex rich
in Lysine and Arginine.

42.explanation_en:
A nucleosome consists of negatively charged
DNA wrapped around a core of eight positively
charged histone proteins called a histone octamer.
Important Facts:
➤ DNA carries a net negative charge due to the pres-
ence of phosphate groups along its sugar-phosphate
backbone.
➤ Histones are basic proteins rich in the positively
charged amino acid residues lysine and arginine.
➤ The histone octamer contains two molecules each of
four core histones: H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
➤ A typical nucleosome wraps approximately 200
base pairs (bp) of DNA around the histone core.
➤ Nucleosomes in chromatin give a characteristic
"beads-on-a-string" appearance under an electron
microscope.

43.question_text_en:
The LVM3 rocket employed for the CMS-03 mission
is classified under which launch vehicle class?
43.question_text_hi:
The LVM3 rocket employed for the CMS-03 mission
is classified under which launch vehicle class?
43.explanation_en:
ISRO's LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3), formerly known
as GSLV Mk III, is classified as a Heavy lift launch
vehicle designed to carry heavy communication satel-
lites.
Important Facts:
➤ LVM3 is a three-stage launch vehicle with two solid
strap-on motors (S200), a core liquid stage (L110), and
a cryogenic upper stage (C25).
➤ It has the capacity to launch payloads of up to 4,000
kg into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
➤ For Low Earth Orbit (LEO), LVM3 can deliver pay-
loads of approximately 8,000 kg.
➤ The vehicle successfully executed prestigious mis-
sions including Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3,
and OneWeb commercial deployments.
➤ It is the designated launch vehicle for India's indige-
nous crewed spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan.

45.question_text_en:
Geoengineering refers to large-scale interventions in
which system to intentionally cool the planet?
45.question_text_hi:
Geoengineering refers to large-scale interventions in
which system to intentionally cool the planet?
45.explanation_en:
Geoengineering refers to deliberate, large-scale tech-
nological interventions directly into the Earth's cli-
mate system to counteract anthropogenic global
warming and cool the planet.
Important Facts:
➤ Geoengineering approaches are broadly divided into
Solar Radiation Management (SRM) and
Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR).
➤ SRM seeks to reflect a small fraction of sunlight back
into space using techniques like stratospheric aerosol in-
jection.
➤ CDR technologies aim to sequester greenhouse
gases directly through afforestation, bioenergy with car-
bon capture, and direct air capture.
➤ Major international bodies, including the IPCC, eval-
uate geoengineering as potential supplementary re-
sponses with notable ecological risks.
➤ The concept was discussed as early as the mid-20th
century, gaining renewed prominence amid accelerating
global climate shifts.

46.question_text_en: Chabahar Port is located in which country?

southeastern Iran, on the Gulf of Oman. It provides
India an alternative transit route to Afghanistan and
Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
Important Facts:

Province of Iran along the Makran coast.

Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar Port.
➤ It is an integral link in the International North–
South Transport Corridor (INSTC) network.
➤ India commenced development of the port following a
bilateral agreement first conceptualized in 2003.
➤ It provides direct maritime access to landlocked
Afghanistan without passing through overland
Pakistani routes.

the World Happiness Report?
50.explanation_en:
The World Happiness Report measures subjective
well-being using the Cantril Ladder question, asking
respondents to evaluate their lives on a ladder scale
from 0 to 10.
Important Facts:
➤ The scale was originally created by social researcher
Hadley Cantril in 1965.
➤ On this ladder scale, 10 represents the best possible
life and 0 represents the worst possible life.
➤ The World Happiness Report is released by the UN
Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
➤ The survey data used for evaluating the rankings is
gathered by the Gallup World Poll.
➤ Key variables assessed alongside the ladder include
GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy,
freedom, generosity, and corruption perceptions.

gymnastics is the Fédération Internationale de
Gymnastique (FIG), founded in 1881.

gymnast to compete at the Olympic Games at Rio
2016.

are present.

the court during active play.

men's kabaddi except in 2018.

29.question_text_en:
Which factor determines the pitch of sound in Tat
Vadya?
29.question_text_hi:
Which factor determines the pitch of sound in Tat
Vadya?
29.explanation_en:
In Tat Vadya (chordophones or stringed instruments),
the fundamental pitch depends on the physical proper-

ties of the vibrating string, primarily its tension, length,
and linear mass density.
Important Facts:
➤ Tat Vadya is the classification for stringed instru-
ments in the ancient Indian classification from the
Natya Shastra.
➤ Increasing the tension of a string increases its fre-
quency of vibration, thereby raising the pitch.
➤ Examples of Tat Vadya include the Sitar, Veena,
Sarod, and Tanpura.
➤ Bharata Muni's *Natya Shastra* divides musical in-
struments into four classes: Tat (stringed),
Avanaddha (percussion), Ghana (solid), and
Sushira (wind).
➤ The fundamental frequency $f$ of a vibrating
stretched string is given by $f = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}
{\mu}}$, showing direct dependence on tension ($T$).

nantly in Sopana sangeetham style using
Manipravalam.

Kerala Kalamandalam.

beer?

as the "100-drum dance" is celebrated with traditional rice

drums called Dama by a hundred drummers simultane-

shared and consumed during the festival.
➤ It marks the end of the agricultural period and agricul-
tural labor in the Garo Hills.
➤ Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland,
while Moatsu is celebrated by the Ao Naga
community.

lakh and Rs1 crore for setting up greenfield enter-
prises.

women categories.
➤ The scheme covers manufacturing, services, agri-al-
lied activities, and the trading sector.
➤ It is administered under the Department of
Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance.

35.question_text_en:
How are the drapery and dress of the Buddha
depicted in the Gandhara School of Art?
35.question_text_hi:
How are the drapery and dress of the Buddha
depicted in the Gandhara School of Art?
35.explanation_en:
The Gandhara School of Art was strongly influ-
enced by Greco-Roman styles, depicting the Buddha
wearing heavy drapery with many realistic, wavy
folds similar to a Roman toga.
Important Facts:
➤ The Gandhara School of Art flourished primarily
under the patronage of the Kushana dynasty, espe-
cially King Kanishka.
➤ It is famously known as the Greco-Buddhist style
of art.
➤ Buddha images in Gandhara art feature wavy hair,
sharp facial contours, and realistic heavy drapery with
deeply carved folds.
➤ The primary material utilized in Gandhara sculptures
was grey sandstone and stucco.
➤ In contrast, the indigenous Mathura School de-
picted Buddha with tight-fitting, transparent drapery.

36.question_text_en: National income is:
36.question_text_hi: National income is:

options.text_en: Total value of goods and services produced in a country
options.text_hi: Total value of goods and services produced in a country

36.explanation_en:
National income is defined as the total net money
value of all final goods and services produced by a
country's normal residents during a given financial year
(Net National Product at factor cost).
Important Facts:
➤ Technically, National Income corresponds to Net
National Product at Factor Cost ($NNP_{FC}$).
➤ It can be measured through three methods:
Production (Output) Method, Income Method,
and Expenditure Method.
➤ Dadabhai Naoroji made the first attempt to esti-
mate India's national income in 1867–68 in his book
*Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*.
➤ The first scientific estimation of national income in
India was conducted by Prof. V.K.R.V. Rao in 1931–
32.
➤ In India, national income statistics are compiled and
released by the National Statistics Office (NSO)
under MoSPI.

37.question_text_en:
Which section under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
addresses crimes against women?
37.question_text_hi:
Which section under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
addresses crimes against women?
37.explanation_en:
Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS),
Section 69 specifically penalises sexual intercourse by
deceitful means or false promises of marriage. Chapter
V of BNS deals extensively with offences against women
and children.
Important Facts:
➤ Section 69 of BNS penalises sexual intercourse
through deceitful means or false promises of em-
ployment, promotion, or marriage.
➤ The offense under Section 69 is punishable with
imprisonment for up to 10 years along with a fine.
➤ The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 re-
placed the historic Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
➤ Chapter V of the BNS is titled "Of Offences
Against Woman and Child".
➤ The new criminal laws in India officially came into ef-
fect on 1 July 2024.

38.question_text_hi:

community temporarily?

Uttarakhand explicitly exempts members of the
Scheduled Tribes (STs) from its purview in accor-
dance with constitutional protections.
Important Facts:
➤ Uttarakhand became the first state in independent

February 2024.

to members of Scheduled Tribes defined under
Article 366(25).
➤ Article 44 of the Indian Constitution contains the
Directive Principle for a Uniform Civil Code.

committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge
Ranjana Prakash Desai.
➤ Goa was previously the only state with a common
civil code, retained from the Portuguese Civil Code of
1867.

Haldia (1,620 km).

40.question_text_en:
Which part of the neuron is responsible for acquiring
information from the environment?
40.question_text_hi:
Which part of the neuron is responsible for acquiring
information from the environment?
40.explanation_en:
Information in a nerve cell is first acquired at the special-
ized dendritic tip (dendrite) of a neuron, where envi-
ronmental stimuli trigger a chemical reaction setting off

an electrical impulse.
Important Facts:
➤ Dendrites receive sensory signals and convert
them into electrical impulses transmitted toward the cell
body.
➤ The electrical impulse travels from the dendrite to the
cell body (cyton) and then along the axon.
➤ At the axon terminal, the electrical signal triggers the
release of chemical neurotransmitters across the
synapse.
➤ Neurons are the fundamental structural and func-
tional units of the nervous system.
➤ The myelin sheath insulates the axon and acceler-
ates electrical impulse transmission.

mission?
41.question_text_hi:
Which satellite was launched as part of the LVM3-M5
mission?
41.explanation_en:

an advanced communication satellite, designated under
the CMS (Communication Satellite) series such as
CMS-03, into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.
Important Facts:
➤ LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3), formerly known as
GSLV Mk III, is ISRO's heaviest operational launch
vehicle.
➤ LVM3 is a three-stage launch vehicle featuring two
solid strap-on motors (S200), a core liquid stage
(L110), and a cryogenic upper stage (C25).
➤ It has a payload capacity of up to 4,000 kg to
Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
➤ LVM3 was the launch vehicle utilized for India's his-
toric Chandrayaan-3 mission (LVM3-M4).
➤ The vehicle is also designated to carry Indian astro-
nauts into space under the Gaganyaan programme.

42.question_text_en: The primary objective of Aditya-L1 is to:
42.question_text_hi: The primary objective of Aditya-L1 is to:

options.text_en: Study solar activities and their impact
options.text_hi: Study solar activities and their impact

42.explanation_en:
Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated space-based solar
mission designed to observe and study solar activities,
including solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and their
impact on space weather.
Important Facts:
➤ Aditya-L1 was launched by ISRO using the PSLV-
C57 rocket on 2 September 2023.
➤ The spacecraft is placed in a halo orbit around the
Lagrangian point 1 (L1), located approximately 1.5
million km from Earth.
➤ Its primary payloads include the Visible Emission
Line Coronagraph (VELC) and SUIT (Solar
Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope).
➤ L1 allows an uninterrupted, continuous view of the
Sun without any occultation or eclipses.
➤ The mission helps study the physics of the solar
corona, coronal heating, and space weather drivers.

tween 1976 and 1997.

the Department of Atomic Energy.

the Indian space programme.

pectancy, freedom, generosity, and absence of
corruption.

96.question_text_en:
In the modern digital age, the shift toward algorithmic
governance suggests a world where human bias is
replaced by the cold, mathematical precision of code.
From credit scoring to judicial sentencing, automated
systems are being integrated into the very fabric of
institutional decision-making. The promise is one of
efficiency and radical neutrality, (A) away the subjective
whims of human administrators.
However, this perceived neutrality is often illusory;
algorithms are, after all, trained on historical data that
inevitably (B) the prejudices of the past. If the training data
contains systemic biases against certain demographics,
the machine learns those patterns as "truths". Far from
eliminating discrimination, the algorithm may simply hide it
behind a veneer of technical objectivity.
Should a predictive policing system be designed to identify
high-risk neighbourhoods, it might inadvertently codify and
amplify existing systemic inequalities. By targeting areas
that were already over-policed due to historical bias, the
system creates a feedback loop. The "math" then appears
to justify the (C) targeting of those same communities,
creating a cycle that is difficult to break.
(D) these tools offer undeniable efficiency in processing
vast amounts of data, they lack the "moral imagination"
required for true justice. A machine can identify a statistical
correlation, but it cannot understand the nuance of human
circumstance or the socio-economic context behind a data
point. It treats humans as static variables rather than
evolving individuals.
This creates a dangerous (E) where the pursuit of
objective fairness results in the automated replication of
historical harm. As we outsource our judgement to
software, we risk losing the ability to hold systems
accountable. We must ensure that the drive for
technological progress does not come at the expense of
the very equity we seek to achieve.
Which word best completes blank (A) to show the effect of
'radical neutrality'?

27.question_text_en:
Sound in Avanaddha Vadya is produced mainly by
vibrating:
27.question_text_hi:
Sound in Avanaddha Vadya is produced mainly by
vibrating:
27.explanation_en:
In the Natyashastra classification of musical instruments,
Avanaddha Vadya (membranophones) produce
sound through the vibration of a stretched animal hide or
membrane struck by hand or stick.
Important Facts:
➤ Ancient Indian musicological treatises classify instru-
ments into four broad categories (Vadya).
➤ Tata Vadya refers to chordophones produced by
vibrating strings (e.g., Veena, Sitar).
➤ Sushira Vadya represents aerophones played by
blown air columns (e.g., Flute, Shehnai).
➤ Ghana Vadya comprises idiophones made of solid
resonance metals or wood (e.g., Manjira, Ghatam).
➤ Common examples of Avanaddha Vadya include the
Tabla, Mridangam, Dholak, and Pakhawaj.

28.question_text_en:
Which of the following activities is Naatupura
Paadalgal, a form of folk music, mainly associated with?
28.question_text_hi:
Which of the following activities is Naatupura
Paadalgal, a form of folk music, mainly associated with?
28.explanation_en:
Naatupura Paadalgal represents Tamil rural folk
songs, traditionally sung by agricultural laborers and
farmers to relieve fatigue and celebrate farming sea-
sons, sowing, and harvesting.
Important Facts:
➤ Naatupura Paadalgal literally translates to "folk
songs" or songs of the rural countryside in Tamil Nadu.
➤ These songs are deeply intertwined with agricultural
activities such as ploughing, transplanting paddy,
and harvesting.
➤ They are also performed during Tamil folk festivals
like Pongal, an agricultural harvest festival.
➤ The lyrics describe rural everyday life, nature, com-
munity relationships, and seasonal changes.
➤ Traditional folk percussion instruments like the
Urumi, Thavil, and Parai often accompany rural
Tamil songs.

29.question_text_en:
The 'SHRESHTA' scheme is designed to provide high-
quality education to meritorious students belonging to
which category?
29.question_text_hi:
The 'SHRESHTA' scheme is designed to provide high-
quality education to meritorious students belonging to
which category?
29.explanation_en:
The SHRESHTA (Scheme for Residential Education for
Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas) was
launched to provide seats for meritorious Scheduled
Caste (SC) students in the country's best private resi-
dential schools.
Important Facts:
➤ The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of
Social Justice and Empowerment.
➤ It provides full funding for school fees and residential
charges from Class 9 to 12.
➤ Selection of beneficiaries is conducted through the
NETS entrance exam conducted by NTA.
➤ Students belonging to families with an annual income
up to Rs2.5 lakh are eligible.
➤ Its objective is to bridge the educational gap and en-
hance socio-economic mobility for SC students.

The 'Hawa Mahal' in Jaipur was designed by Lal
Chand Ustad. What was its primary architectural purpose?

The 'Hawa Mahal' in Jaipur was designed by Lal
Chand Ustad. What was its primary architectural purpose?

options.text_en: To serve as a military watchtower
options.text_hi: To serve as a military watchtower

options.text_en:
To allow royal ladies to observe street festivities without
being seen
options.text_hi:
To allow royal ladies to observe street festivities without
being seen

options.text_en: To act as a giant cooling system for the city
options.text_hi: To act as a giant cooling system for the city

30.explanation_en:
Built under strict purdah customs, the Hawa Mahal fea-
tured 953 small latticed windows (Jharokhas) so that
royal women could watch daily street life and
royal processions from inside without being seen by
the public.
Important Facts:
➤ Hawa Mahal was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai
Pratap Singh.
➤ Its unique five-storey exterior resembles the honey-
comb of a beehive and is shaped like the crown of Lord
Krishna.
➤ It was architecturally designed by Lal Chand
Ustad using red and pink sandstone.
➤ It has 953 intricately carved
casements/windows (Jharokhas) that circulate
cool breeze via the Venturi effect.
➤ The structure stands without a formal solid foundation

and is the world's tallest building constructed without
one.

31.explanation_en:
A celt is a prehistoric stone tool or implement, specifi-
cally a polished or ground stone axe or adze head widely
used during the Neolithic period for woodworking and
agricultural tasks.
Important Facts:
➤ Celts were typically manufactured from hard stones
such as basalt, jadeite, or flint.
➤ They were finished with grinding and polishing,
characteristic hallmarks of Neolithic tool technology.
➤ Celts were hafted onto wooden handles and used for
clearing forests, tilling soil, and carpentry.
➤ Major Indian Neolithic sites yielding celts include
Burzahom (Kashmir) and Brahmagiri
(Karnataka).
➤ The appearance of celts marks the transition from
hunting-gathering to sedentary agriculture.

32.question_text_en:
Where were female figures most prominently depicted
in the Mathura style on stupa architecture?
32.question_text_hi:
Where were female figures most prominently depicted
in the Mathura style on stupa architecture?
32.explanation_en:
In Mathura Buddhist art, female figures—such as
Yakshis, Salabhanjikas, and river goddesses—were
prominently carved in high relief on the upright pillars of
stone railings (Vedika) surrounding stupas.
Important Facts:
➤ The Mathura school flourished under the patronage
of the Kushana Empire (1st to 3rd century CE).
➤ Railing pillars (Vedika stambhas) at Kankali Tila
and Bhuteshwar feature sensuous Yakshi sculptures.
➤ Mathura sculptures were predominantly carved out of
local spotted red sandstone.
➤ Stupa components include the hemispherical dome
(Anda), square balcony (Harmika), and umbrella
(Chhatri).
➤ Mathura art is celebrated for developing indigenous
representations of Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu deities.

movement?

Assertion of an alternative religious framework challenging

options.text_hi: Complete indifference to questions of death and afterlife

options.text_hi: Dependence on orthodox texts for legitimising new practices

33.explanation_en:
By burying their dead instead of cremating and discard-
ing Brahmanical post-death pollution rituals, the

Lingayats under Basavanna deliberately established an
alternative egalitarian religious framework
that contested Vedic and Dharmashastric ritual hierar-
chies.
Important Facts:
➤ The Virashaiva/Lingayat movement was initi-
ated in 12th-century Karnataka by Basavanna (along
with Allama Prabhu and Akka Mahadevi).
➤ Lingayats bury their dead because they believe the
devotee is instantly reunited with Shiva upon death
without rebirth.
➤ The movement rejected caste discrimination, idol
worship, animal sacrifice, and the authority of the
Vedas.
➤ Basavanna's followers expressed their spiritual and
social philosophy through vernacular devotional poems
called Vachanas.
➤ Basavanna established the Anubhava Mantapa,
an open socio-spiritual parliament welcoming people of
all castes and genders.

34.question_text_en:
Which of the following is an example of a Giffen
good?
34.question_text_hi:
Which of the following is an example of a Giffen
good?
34.explanation_en:
Bajra (millet) is a staple coarse grain consumed by
low-income households, serving as a classic example of
an inferior or Giffen good. For a Giffen good, an in-
crease in its price leads to an increase in quantity de-
manded because consumers cannot afford superior sub-
stitutes.
Important Facts:
➤ Giffen goods are rare, highly inferior goods that vio-
late the Law of Demand.

➤ The concept was introduced by Scottish economist
Sir Robert Giffen.
➤ The income effect for a Giffen good is negative
and strongly outweighs the substitution effect.
➤ The demand curve for a Giffen good is upward
sloping.
➤ Staple low-cost carbohydrates like coarse grains or
potatoes commonly illustrate Giffen behavior.

35.question_text_en: What is understood by Fiscal Deficit?
35.question_text_hi: What is understood by Fiscal Deficit?

options.text_en:
Excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding
borrowings
options.text_hi:
Excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding
borrowings

options.text_en: Excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.text_hi: Excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts

35.explanation_en:
Fiscal Deficit is defined as the excess of total govern-
ment expenditure over total receipts excluding borrow-

ings, representing the total amount of money the govern-
ment needs to borrow in a financial year.
Important Facts:
➤ Formula: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure −
(Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital
Receipts).
➤ It reflects the total borrowing requirement of
the government from all domestic and external sources.
➤ Revenue Deficit is the difference between rev-
enue expenditure and revenue receipts.
➤ Primary Deficit is calculated as Fiscal Deficit mi-
nus interest payments (Primary Deficit = Fiscal
Deficit − Interest Payments).
➤ The FRBM Act, 2003 was enacted in India to insti-
tutionalize fiscal discipline and reduce deficits.

36.question_text_en:
Which Five-Year Plan proposed the main objectives of
'removal of poverty' and 'attainment of self reliance'?
36.question_text_hi:
Which Five-Year Plan proposed the main objectives of
'removal of poverty' and 'attainment of self reliance'?
36.explanation_en:
The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979) focused on
two primary objectives: Garibi Hatao (Removal of
Poverty) and the attainment of economic self-reliance.
Important Facts:
➤ The Fifth Plan was drafted and launched under the
leadership of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
➤ It introduced the Minimum Needs Programme
(MNP) in 1974 to provide basic social amenities.
➤ The plan was terminated a year early in 1978 by the
newly elected Janata Party government.
➤ It was followed by the Rolling Plan (1978–1980).
➤ The target growth rate of the Fifth Plan was 4.4%,
and it achieved an actual growth rate of 4.8%.

37.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: The maximum equity limit for
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in most sectors was
______ under the New Economic Policy.
37.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: The maximum equity limit for
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in most sectors was
______ under the New Economic Policy.
37.explanation_en:
Under the New Economic Policy of 1991, India
liberalized its investment regime and significantly in-
creased the foreign equity limits (up to 51% automatic
approval in priority high-technology industries).
Important Facts:
➤ The New Economic Policy was introduced in July
1991 based on Liberalisation, Privatisation, and
Globalisation (LPG).
➤ Before 1991, foreign equity participation was strictly
restricted under the Foreign Exchange Regulation
Act (FERA), 1973.
➤ Automatic approval was granted for foreign direct in-
vestment up to 51% foreign equity in 34 high-priority
sectors.
➤ The Foreign Investment Promotion Board
(FIPB) was established to examine FDI proposals out-
side the automatic route.
➤ These reforms aimed to invite foreign capital, modern
technology, and integrate the Indian economy with global
markets.

38.question_text_en:
Which committee's recommendations formed the
basis for the financial sector reforms in India in 1991?
38.question_text_hi:
Which committee's recommendations formed the
basis for the financial sector reforms in India in 1991?
38.explanation_en:
The Narasimham Committee I (Committee on
the Financial System) submitted its historic report in
November 1991, laying the blueprint for comprehensive
banking and financial sector reforms in India.
Important Facts:
➤ The committee was chaired by former RBI Governor
M. Narasimham.
➤ It recommended phased reductions in the
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash
Reserve Ratio (CRR).
➤ It recommended the deregulation of interest rates
and introduction of prudential accounting norms.
➤ It proposed capital adequacy norms aligned with in-
ternational standards (Basel Accords).
➤ A second committee under M. Narasimham was con-
stituted in 1998 to recommend banking sector reforms.

39.question_text_en:
Which authority has the power to restrict Fundamental
Rights of armed forces?
39.question_text_hi:
Which authority has the power to restrict Fundamental
Rights of armed forces?
39.explanation_en:
Under Article 33 of the Indian Constitution, only the
Parliament has the constitutional authority to modify
or restrict the application of Fundamental Rights to mem-
bers of the armed forces and related services.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 33 empowers Parliament to determine to
what extent fundamental rights apply to members of the
Armed Forces, paramilitary forces, police, and intelli-
gence agencies.
➤ The power to make laws under Article 33 is vested
exclusively in Parliament, not state legislatures.
➤ The primary purpose is to ensure the proper dis-
charge of their duties and the maintenance of
discipline.
➤ Any law enacted under Article 33 cannot be chal-
lenged in any court on the ground of infringement of fun-
damental rights.
➤ Examples include the Army Act (1950), the Navy
Act (1957), and the Air Force Act (1950).

Parliament has the constitutional authority to modify
or restrict the application of Fundamental Rights to mem-
bers of the armed forces and related services.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 33 empowers Parliament to determine to
what extent fundamental rights apply to members of the
Armed Forces, paramilitary forces, police, and intelli-
gence agencies.
➤ The power to make laws under Article 33 is vested
exclusively in Parliament, not state legislatures.
➤ The primary purpose is to ensure the proper dis-
charge of their duties and the maintenance of
discipline.
➤ Any law enacted under Article 33 cannot be chal-
lenged in any court on the ground of infringement of fun-
damental rights.
➤ Examples include the Army Act (1950), the Navy
Act (1957), and the Air Force Act (1950).

accorded constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj in-
stitutions in India by adding Part IX and the Eleventh
Schedule to the Constitution.
Important Facts:

April 1993, celebrated annually as National
Panchayati Raj Day.

Eleventh Schedule containing 29 functional items.
➤ It mandated a three-tier structure: Gram
Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zilla Parishad.
➤ It introduced mandatory one-third reservation
for women in Panchayati Raj institutions.
➤ The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 simultaneously
granted constitutional status to urban local bodies
(Municipalities).

(CrPC), 1973.

alongside traditional paper documents.

43.question_text_en:
Which type of earthquake waves are similar to sound
waves and can travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid
materials?
43.question_text_hi:
Which type of earthquake waves are similar to sound
waves and can travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid
materials?
43.explanation_en:
P-waves (Primary waves) are longitudinal compres-
sional waves similar to sound waves that vibrate parallel
to the direction of propagation and travel through solids,
liquids, and gases.
Important Facts:
➤ P-waves are the fastest seismic waves and the first
to arrive at seismograph stations.
➤ S-waves (Secondary waves) are transverse
waves that can travel only through solid materials.
➤ The inability of S-waves to travel through liquids re-
vealed that Earth's outer core is liquid.
➤ P-waves cause particles to compress and dilate in

the direction of wave movement.
➤ Surface waves (Love and Rayleigh waves) travel
along the surface and cause the most severe
destruction.

45.question_text_en:
If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20%
Adenine, what is the expected percentage of Guanine
based on Chargaff's rules?
45.question_text_hi:
If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20%
Adenine, what is the expected percentage of Guanine
based on Chargaff's rules?
45.explanation_en:
According to Chargaff's rules, Adenine equals Thymine
(A = T = 20%, total 40%). The remaining bases Guanine
and Cytosine constitute 60% together, and since G = C,
Guanine is 30% (60% / 2).
Important Facts:
➤ Chargaff's rules were formulated by biochemist
Erwin Chargaff in the late 1940s.
➤ The rule states that in double-stranded DNA, the ratio
of purines to pyrimidines is 1:1 (A + G = T + C).
➤ Adenine pairs with Thymine via two hydrogen
bonds (A=T).
➤ Guanine pairs with Cytosine via three hydrogen
bonds (G≡C).
➤ Chargaff's findings provided critical experimental data
for Watson and Crick's double-helix model of DNA.

Explanation

prove productivity assumes that working from home will

plicit.

earlier → I is not implicit.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit.
✔ Answer: (B)

स्पष्ट.
यह आवश्यक नहीं है कि कर्मचारी कम उत्पादक हों
