The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution con-
tains the legal provisions regarding the disqualifica-
tion of legislators on grounds of defection
(Anti-Defection Law).
Important Facts:
➤ The Tenth Schedule was inserted into the
Constitution by the 52nd Constitutional
Amendment Act, 1985.
➤ The decision on disqualification under the Tenth
Schedule is made by the Speaker or Chairman of
the respective House.
➤ In the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case (1992),
the Supreme Court held that the Presiding Officer's deci-
sion is subject to judicial review.
➤ The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act,
2003 omitted the provision protecting one-third split in a
political party from disqualification.
➤ Articles 102(2) (for Parliament) and 191(2) (for
State Legislatures) link membership disqualification to
the Tenth Schedule.

37.question_text_en:
In the context of astronomy, what is the name of the
galaxy that contains our solar system and billions of other
stars and planetary systems?
37.question_text_hi:
In the context of astronomy, what is the name of the
galaxy that contains our solar system and billions of other
stars and planetary systems?
37.explanation_en:
Our solar system and billions of surrounding stars are
part of the barred spiral galaxy known as the Milky
Way Galaxy (Akash Ganga).
Important Facts:
➤ The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy with a
diameter estimated between 100,000 and 150,000
light-years.
➤ At the centre of the Milky Way lies a supermassive
black hole named Sagittarius A\*.
➤ Our solar system is situated in the Orion-Cygnus
Arm (Orion Arm) of the Milky Way, approximately
26,000 light-years from the galactic centre.
➤ The closest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way is
the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), located about 2.5 mil-
lion light-years away.
➤ The Milky Way and Andromeda belong to a gravita-
tionally bound group of galaxies known as the Local
Group.

38.question_text_en:
What causes the variation in time zones across
different regions of the Earth based on longitudinal
differences?
38.question_text_hi:
What causes the variation in time zones across
different regions of the Earth based on longitudinal
differences?
38.explanation_en:
The rotation of Earth from west to east causes the
Sun to appear to move across the sky, producing a 4-
minute time difference for every 1 degree of longi-
tude.
Important Facts:
➤ The Earth rotates 360 degrees on its axis in ap-
proximately 24 hours, which equals 15 degrees per
hour or 1 degree in 4 minutes.
➤ Places located east of the Prime Meridian (0°
longitude) at Greenwich see the Sun earlier and are
ahead in time.
➤ India's standard time is based on the 82°30' E longi-
tude, which is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of
Greenwich Mean Time (GMT +5:30).
➤ The International Date Line roughly follows the
180° meridian; crossing it westward advances the cal-
endar by one day.
➤ Earth's revolution around the Sun, combined with
its axial tilt, is responsible for the change of seasons, not
daily time zones.

39.question_text_en:
What is the northern-most range of the Himalayas
commonly called?
39.question_text_hi:
What is the northern-most range of the Himalayas
commonly called?
39.explanation_en:
The northern-most and highest continuous range of the
Himalayas is known as the Great Himalayas or
Himadri.
Important Facts:
➤ The Himadri range has an average elevation of
about 6,000 metres above sea level.
➤ It contains all the prominent peaks including Mount
Everest (8,848.86 m) and Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).
➤ The core of the Greater Himalayas is composed pri-
marily of granite.
➤ South of the Himadri lies the Himachal (Lesser or
Middle Himalayas) with an average height between
3,700 and 4,500 metres.
➤ The southernmost outer range of the Himalayas is
the Shiwaliks, composed of unconsolidated
sediments.

from parents to offspring is called:
41.question_text_hi:
The process by which characteristics are transmitted
from parents to offspring is called:
41.explanation_en:
Heredity refers to the biological mechanism by which
genetic traits and characteristics are passed down from
parents to their progeny.
Important Facts:
➤ Gregor Johann Mendel is recognized as the
"Father of Genetics" for his pioneering work on pea
plants (*Pisum sativum*).
➤ Mendel formulated the fundamental laws of inheri-
tance: the Law of Segregation and the Law of
Independent Assortment.
➤ Genes located on chromosomes in DNA are the
functional physical units of heredity.
➤ Variation refers to the morphological and physio-
logical differences exhibited by individuals of the same
species.
➤ Mutation is a sudden, inheritable change in the nu-
cleotide sequence of an organism's genome.

ness.

(ITEWC) is operated by INCOIS in Hyderabad.

44.question_text_en:
The "Krakatoa Mechanism" in climatology refers to
which of the following phenomena?
44.question_text_hi:
The "Krakatoa Mechanism" in climatology refers to
which of the following phenomena?

options.text_en:
The influence of volcanic aerosols in the stratosphere
reflecting solar radiation and causing global cooling.
options.text_hi:
The influence of volcanic aerosols in the stratosphere
reflecting solar radiation and causing global cooling.

options.text_en:
The generation of tsunamis through underwater
earthquakes.
options.text_hi:
The generation of tsunamis through underwater
earthquakes.

options.text_en: The movement of tectonic plates in the Sunda Strait.
options.text_hi: The movement of tectonic plates in the Sunda Strait.

options.text_en: The impact of sound waves on cloud seeding.
options.text_hi: The impact of sound waves on cloud seeding.

44.explanation_en:
The Krakatoa Mechanism refers to large explosive
volcanic eruptions injecting sulfur dioxide aerosols
into the stratosphere, which backscatter solar insolation
and cause temporary global cooling.
Important Facts:
➤ The phenomenon is named after the colossal erup-
tion of the Krakatoa (Krakatau) volcano in the
Sunda Strait, Indonesia, in August 1883.
➤ Sulfur dioxide ($SO_2$) gas injected into the strato-
sphere oxidizes to form reflective sulfate aerosol
veils.
➤ Because the stratosphere lacks weather and pre-
cipitation, these aerosols can persist for 1 to 3 years.
➤ The 1883 Krakatoa eruption caused global tempera-
tures to drop by approximately 1.2°C in the subsequent
year.
➤ A similar planetary cooling effect was documented
following the eruption of Mount Pinatubo (Philippines)
in 1991.

27.question_text_en:
The "Kharchi Puja" festival is celebrated in which of

27.question_text_hi:
The "Kharchi Puja" festival is celebrated in which of
the following states?
27.explanation_en:
Kharchi Puja is a major Hindu festival celebrated in
the northeastern state of Tripura. The festival involves
the worship of the fourteen deities (Chaturdasha
Devata) over seven consecutive days.
Important Facts:
➤ Kharchi Puja is celebrated annually at the
Chaturdasha Devata Temple in Old Agartala.
➤ It is observed in the month of Ashadha (usually fall-
ing in July).
➤ The ritual marks the cleansing and purification of
Mother Earth (Ama Pechi).
➤ The chief royal priest who oversees the sacred rituals
is known as the Chantai.
➤ Although originally a royal tribal festival of the
Tripuri people, it is now celebrated across all
communities.

30.question_text_en:
In the later phase of the Gandhara School of art,
which group of materials was primarily used for making
sculptures instead of blue-grey schist stone?
30.question_text_hi:
In the later phase of the Gandhara School of art,
which group of materials was primarily used for making
sculptures instead of blue-grey schist stone?
30.explanation_en:
While the early phase of the Gandhara School predomi-
nantly utilized blue-grey schist stone, its later
phase (around the 3rd to 5th centuries CE) saw wide-
spread adoption of mud, lime, and stucco (plaster)
along with clay for sculpting Buddha figures.
Important Facts:
➤ The Gandhara School of Art developed in north-
western ancient India during the rule of the Kushana
dynasty.
➤ It is famously characterized as a Greco-Buddhist
style combining Hellenistic sculptural techniques with
Buddhist themes.
➤ Stucco allowed artists greater plasticity and speed
in crafting intricate facial expressions and drapery folds.
➤ Major centres of the Gandhara school included
Taxila, Peshawar, Begram, and Hadda.
➤ Unlike Gandhara art, the contemporary Mathura
School of Art primarily utilized spotted red sandstone.

ciency of PSUs.

along with management control, it is termed Strategic
Disinvestment.

of the Ministry of Finance.

33.question_text_en:
Which constitutional feature ensures accountability of
executive through requirement that it must enjoy
confidence of lower house of legislature?
33.question_text_hi:
Which constitutional feature ensures accountability of
executive through requirement that it must enjoy
confidence of lower house of legislature?
33.explanation_en:
In a Parliamentary system, the executive is drawn
directly from the legislature and remains collectively re-
sponsible to the lower house of the legislature (Lok
Sabha in India), retaining power only as long as it enjoys
its majority confidence.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution explicitly
provides that the Council of Ministers is collectively re-
sponsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
➤ A defeat in a No-Confidence Motion forces the
Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers to re-
sign.
➤ India borrowed the parliamentary model of gover-
nance from the British Westminster system.
➤ In a Presidential system (like the USA), the ex-
ecutive is independent of the legislature and not subject
to legislative confidence votes.
➤ The principle of collective responsibility is the
core foundational bedrock of parliamentary democracy.

34.question_text_en:
In the Indian Constitution, which article deals with the
abolition of titles?
34.question_text_hi:
In the Indian Constitution, which article deals with the
abolition of titles?
34.explanation_en:
Article 18 of the Indian Constitution abolishes titles to
ensure social equality, prohibiting the State from confer-
ring any title except military and academic distinctions.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 18(1) bars Indian citizens and foreign nationals
holding any office of profit under the State from accept-
ing titles from foreign countries.
➤ The Supreme Court in the Balaji Raghavan case
(1996) upheld the validity of National Awards (like
Bharat Ratna and Padma awards), ruling they are deco-
rations and not titles.
➤ Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and
equal protection of the laws.
➤ Article 21 protects the Fundamental Right to life
and personal liberty.
➤ Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and
forced labour (begar).

35.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: ______ restricts discussion on the
conduct of Judges in Parliament.
35.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: ______ restricts discussion on the
conduct of Judges in Parliament.
35.explanation_en:
Article 121 of the Indian Constitution prohibits any
discussion in Parliament regarding the conduct of any
Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court in the
discharge of their duties, except upon a motion for pre-
senting an address praying for the removal of the Judge.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 121 ensures the independence of the ju-
diciary by shielding judges from legislative interfer-
ence.
➤ The only exception is during the formal consideration
of an impeachment motion under Article 124(4).
➤ A corresponding restriction applies to State
Legislatures under Article 211 of the Constitution.
➤ Article 120 deals with the language to be used in
Parliament (Hindi or English).
➤ Article 122 prevents courts from inquiring into par-
liamentary proceedings on grounds of alleged proce-
dural irregularity.

36.question_text_en:
Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains
provisions related to the Forms of Oaths or Affirmations?
36.question_text_hi:
Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains
provisions related to the Forms of Oaths or Affirmations?
36.explanation_en:
The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution con-
tains the forms of oaths or affirmations for constitutional
posts including Union and State Ministers, MPs, MLAs,
and Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
Important Facts:
➤ The oaths of the President (Article 60), Vice-
President (Article 69), and Governor (Article 159) are
mentioned directly in their respective articles, not in the
Third Schedule.
➤ The First Schedule lists the names of States and
Union Territories along with their territorial jurisdictions.
➤ The Second Schedule contains provisions relating
to the salaries, allowances, and emoluments of key con-
stitutional dignitaries.
➤ The Fourth Schedule deals with the allocation of
seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
➤ The Indian Constitution originally had 8 Schedules
in 1950, which has now increased to 12 Schedules.

37.question_text_en:
Which factor primarily causes the variation of
seasons on Earth, considering the tilt and movement of
Earth relative to the Sun throughout the year?
37.question_text_hi:
Which factor primarily causes the variation of
seasons on Earth, considering the tilt and movement of
Earth relative to the Sun throughout the year?
37.explanation_en:
The primary cause of seasonal variation on Earth is the
tilt of Earth's axis (at an angle of approximately
23.5 degrees) combined with its revolution around the
Sun, which changes the angle and duration of incoming
solar insolation throughout the year.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth's axis maintains a permanent axial tilt of 66.5
degrees relative to its orbital plane (and 23.5 degrees
from the perpendicular).
➤ When the Northern Hemisphere tilts towards the Sun,
it experiences summer, while the Southern
Hemisphere experiences winter.
➤ Summer Solstice occurs on June 21, when the
Sun's rays fall directly over the Tropic of Cancer.
➤ Winter Solstice occurs on December 22, when
the Sun shines directly over the Tropic of Capricorn.
➤ The slight change in the Earth-Sun distance (perihe-
lion and aphelion) plays only a minor role in seasonal
temperature differences.

38.question_text_en:
Why does the Sun appear to rise in the east and set
in the west when observed from Earth daily?
38.question_text_hi:
Why does the Sun appear to rise in the east and set
in the west when observed from Earth daily?
38.explanation_en:
The apparent daily motion of the Sun rising in the east
and setting in the west is caused by the rotation of
Earth from west to east on its polar axis.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth completes one full rotation on its axis in ap-
proximately 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 sec-
onds (one sidereal day).
➤ Because Earth spins towards the east, celestial bod-
ies in space appear to move across the sky towards the
west.
➤ Rotation of Earth is the fundamental cause of the cy-
cle of day and night.
➤ In our solar system, Venus and Uranus rotate in a
retrograde (east-to-west) direction, opposite to Earth.
➤ The rotational speed of Earth at the equator is ap-
proximately 1,670 km/h (about 460 m/s).

options.text_en:

39.explanation_en:
During a strong La Niña event, unusually cold waters in
the eastern Pacific strengthen the trade winds and drive
warm waters westward, causing enhanced convec-
tion over the Western Pacific/Indonesia, which
invigorates the ascending branch of the Walker cell and
typically strengthens the Indian monsoon.
Important Facts:
➤ La Niña represents the cold phase of the El Niño–
Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle.
➤ In contrast, El Niño events are associated with
warmer central/eastern Pacific waters and frequently
cause monsoon droughts in India.
➤ The Walker Circulation is a vast east-west atmo-
spheric circulation pattern along the tropical Pacific
ocean.
➤ La Niña conditions often result in above-normal rain-
fall and colder winter conditions across Northern India.
➤ The phenomenon of cooler-than-average sea surface
temperatures during La Niña leads to an elevated ther-
mocline in the eastern Pacific.

40.question_text_en: What is another name for the Outer Himalayas?
40.question_text_hi: What is another name for the Outer Himalayas?
40.explanation_en:
The outermost and southernmost range of the
Himalayan mountain system is known as the Shiwalik
Mountain Range (or Outer Himalayas). They are
composed of unconsolidated sediments brought down
by rivers from the higher ranges.
Important Facts:
➤ The Shiwaliks have an average altitude varying be-
tween 900 and 1,100 metres.
➤ Their average width ranges between 10 and 50
km.
➤ Longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser
Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called Duns (e.g.,
Dehradun, Kotli Dun).
➤ The Himadri refers to the Greater or Inner
Himalayas, which contain the highest peaks.
➤ The Himachal range represents the Lesser or
Middle Himalayas, lying between the Himadri and
the Shiwalik.

43.question_text_en: 'Cuscuta' (amar-bel) shows which type of nutrition?
43.question_text_hi: 'Cuscuta' (amar-bel) shows which type of nutrition?
43.explanation_en:
Cuscuta (commonly known as Amar-bel) exhibits par-
asitic nutrition. It lacks chlorophyll and cannot syn-
thesize its own food through photosynthesis, deriving
ready-made nutrients directly from the host plant.
Important Facts:
➤ Cuscuta is classified as an obligate stem
holoparasite.
➤ It absorbs water and essential nutrients from the host
plant using specialized root-like structures called haus-
toria.
➤ Since it lacks green pigment (chlorophyll), it can-
not perform autotrophic nutrition.
➤ Parasitic plants can severely reduce the vitality,
growth, and yield of their host plants.
➤ Organisms that feed on decaying organic matter (like
fungi) are called saprophytes.

44.explanation_en:
The CBDR-RC principle establishes that while all na-
tions share a common duty to protect the environment,
developed nations must take the lead in mitiga-
tion and finance because of their historical responsibility
for cumulative emissions and greater financial capabili-
ties.
Important Facts:
➤ The CBDR principle was formally enshrined in
Principle 7 of the 1992 Rio Declaration on
Environment and Development.
➤ It was adopted as a core foundational pillar of the
United Nations Framework Convention on
Climate Change (UNFCCC).
➤ Under the Kyoto Protocol (1997), binding emis-
sion reduction targets were imposed exclusively on de-
veloped (Annex I) countries.
➤ The 2015 Paris Agreement reaffirmed CBDR-RC
while introducing nationally determined contributions
(NDCs) for all nations.

➤ Developed countries are legally obliged under this
framework to provide climate finance and technology
transfer to developing states.

49.explanation_en:
Under Component-A of the PM-KUSUM scheme, indi-
vidual farmers, cooperatives, and panchayats can install
decentralized ground-mounted solar power plants (up to
2 MW) on barren or cultivable lands and sell the gen-
erated electricity to local DISCOMs at a prede-
termined feed-in tariff.
Important Facts:
➤ The PM-KUSUM scheme was launched in 2019
by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
➤ Component-B focuses on the installation of stand-
alone solar agriculture pumps for individual farmers.
➤ Component-C provides support for solarizing exist-
ing grid-connected agricultural pumps (including feeder
level solarization).
➤ Component-A aims to generate steady supplemen-
tary income for farmers from unused or fallow land.
➤ Power distribution companies (DISCOMs) purchase
this renewable energy to meet their Renewable
Purchase Obligations (RPO).

of modern technology to students, engineers, and
builders.

stones for the six Lighthouse Projects on January 1,
2021.

Work backwards (each checkpoint: x → x/2 + 2):

After 2nd: 16 → 16 − 2 = 14 → 14 × 2 = 28
After 1st: 28 → 28 − 2 = 26 → 26 × 2 = 52
Answer: 52 apples

26.question_text_en: What is the standard shape of a basketball?
26.question_text_hi: What is the standard shape of a basketball?
26.explanation_en:
A basketball is a three-dimensional object manufactured
strictly in a spherical geometry to ensure uniform
bounce, roll, and aerodynamic balance.
Important Facts:
➤ The standard regulation basketball has an official cir-
cumference of 29.5 inches (75 cm) for men's profes-
sional play (Size 7).
➤ Basketball was invented in December 1891 by
Canadian physical educator Dr. James Naismith in
Springfield, Massachusetts.
➤ The global governing body for the sport of basketball
is FIBA (International Basketball Federation), founded
in 1932.
➤ Basketball was introduced as an official men's
Olympic medal sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
➤ The standard height of the rim (hoop) above the court
floor is exactly 10 feet (3.05 metres).

27.question_text_en:
"Chapchar Kut" is a vibrant spring festival associated
with which Indian state?
27.question_text_hi:
"Chapchar Kut" is a vibrant spring festival associated
with which Indian state?
27.explanation_en:
Chapchar Kut is the most prominent spring festival
celebrated by the Mizo people of Mizoram, marking the
completion of jhum (slash-and-burn) clearing.
Important Facts:
➤ The festival is celebrated annually in the month of
March after clearing jungle clearings for cultivation.
➤ A signature highlight of Chapchar Kut is the traditional
Cheraw dance (popularly known as the bamboo
dance).
➤ Traditional attire, folk music, and community feasts
are central to the celebrations.
➤ Other prominent agricultural festivals in Mizoram in-
clude Mim Kut and Pawl Kut.
➤ Mizoram attained full statehood as the 23rd state of
the Indian Union on 20 February 1987.

28.question_text_en:
From 2001 to 2011, what was the decline in India's
average annual growth rate of population?
28.question_text_hi:
From 2001 to 2011, what was the decline in India's
average annual growth rate of population?
28.explanation_en:
India's average annual exponential population growth
rate dropped from 1.97% during 1991–2001 to 1.64%
during 2001–2011, reflecting a decline of 0.32% (or
~0.33 percentage points).
Important Facts:
➤ The decadal growth rate of India's population during
2001–2011 was 17.7%, down from 21.5% in 1991–
2001.
➤ According to the Census 2011, India's total popula-
tion stood at approximately 1.21 billion (121.08
crore).
➤ Nagaland was the only Indian state to record a
negative population growth rate (−0.58%) during the
2001–2011 decade.
➤ Meghalaya registered the highest decadal popula-
tion growth rate among Indian states at 27.95%.
➤ The year 1921 is termed the 'Year of the Great
Divide' in Indian demographic history because popula-
tion growth turned permanently positive thereafter.

29.question_text_en:
St. Philomena's Church in Mysore is an example of
which architectural style?
29.question_text_hi:
St. Philomena's Church in Mysore is an example of
which architectural style?
29.explanation_en:
St. Philomena's Cathedral in Mysuru (Mysore),
Karnataka, is built in the Neo-Gothic architectural
style, inspired by the Cologne Cathedral in Germany.
Important Facts:
➤ Constructed in 1936, the church was designed by a
French architect named Daly during the reign of
Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV.
➤ The cathedral features towering twin spires that rise
to a height of 175 feet (53 metres).
➤ Its twin spires and stained-glass windows depicting
events from the life of Christ are classic hallmarks of
Gothic Revival (Neo-Gothic) architecture.
➤ The church was erected in honour of Saint
Philomena, a 4th-century Greek saint and martyr.
➤ Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV laid the foundation stone of
the present cathedral structure in October 1933.

30.question_text_en:
Which of the Five-Year Plan had a target growth rate
of 5.2% and an actual growth rate of 5.7%?
30.question_text_hi:
Which of the Five-Year Plan had a target growth rate
of 5.2% and an actual growth rate of 5.7%?
30.explanation_en:
The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985) targeted a
GDP growth rate of 5.2% and successfully achieved an
actual growth rate of 5.7% (or 5.66%).
Important Facts:
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan marked the beginning
of economic liberalisation in India, focusing on poverty
eradication (Garibi Hatao) and technological self-re-
liance.
➤ Key rural development initiatives such as the
Integrated Rural Development Programme
(IRDP) and NREP were expanded during this plan.
➤ NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural
Development) was established on 12 July 1982 dur-
ing the Sixth Plan.
➤ The EXIM Bank of India was also set up in 1982
under this plan to boost foreign trade.
➤ India's Five-Year Plans were formulated by the
Planning Commission, which was replaced by NITI
Aayog on 1 January 2015.

31.question_text_en:
Which of the following industries still requires
industrial licensing?
31.question_text_hi:
Which of the following industries still requires
industrial licensing?
31.explanation_en:
Following the 1991 economic reforms, compulsory in-
dustrial licensing was abolished for most sectors,
but remains mandatory for a few sensitive industries, in-
cluding hazardous chemicals.
Important Facts:
➤ Compulsory licensing is currently retained for only a
few items, including defence aerospace and war-
ships, industrial explosives, and specified haz-
ardous chemicals.
➤ The landmark New Industrial Policy of 24 July
1991 drastically reduced the number of industries re-
quiring licensing to promote delicensing and deregula-
tion.
➤ Industries involving atomic energy and railway trans-
port operations remain strictly reserved for the public
sector.

➤ Industrial licensing in India is administered under the
provisions of the Industries (Development and
Regulation) Act, 1951 (IDRA).
➤ Delicensing eliminated red tape, allowing domestic
and foreign investment to flow freely into consumer sec-
tors like textiles and automobiles.

32.question_text_en:
Which Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to
the "Right to Freedom of Religion"?
32.question_text_hi:
Which Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to
the "Right to Freedom of Religion"?
32.explanation_en:
The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed
as a Fundamental Right under Articles 25 to 28 in
Part III of the Constitution of India.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and
free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
➤ Article 26 grants the freedom to manage religious
affairs.
➤ Article 27 provides freedom from the payment of
taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
➤ Article 28 guarantees freedom regarding atten-
dance at religious instruction or worship in certain edu-
cational institutions.
➤ The word 'Secular' was explicitly inserted into the
Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd
Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

33.question_text_en:
Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains
provisions related to the President and Governors of
States?
33.question_text_hi:
Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains
provisions related to the President and Governors of
States?
33.explanation_en:
The Second Schedule of the Constitution of India
contains provisions relating to the emoluments, al-
lowances, and privileges of the President,
Governors of States, Judges, and other high consti-
tutional authorities.
Important Facts:
➤ Part A of the Second Schedule specifically deals
with provisions as to the President and the
Governors of States.
➤ The Third Schedule contains the forms of Oaths
or Affirmations for ministers, judges, and legislators.
➤ The First Schedule lists the names of the States
and Union Territories and their territorial jurisdic-
tions.
➤ The Fourth Schedule specifies the allocation of
seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
➤ The original Indian Constitution contained 8
Schedules, whereas it currently has 12 Schedules.

34.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: Article ______ of the Constitution
relates to the language used in Parliament.
34.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: Article ______ of the Constitution
relates to the language used in Parliament.
34.explanation_en:
Article 120 of the Constitution of India contains provi-
sions specifically governing the language to be used
in Parliament (Hindi or English, with permission for
mother tongue).
Important Facts:
➤ Article 120 provides that business in Parliament
shall be transacted in Hindi or in English, subject to
the Presiding Officer's permission to address in one's
mother tongue.
➤ Correspondingly, Article 210 governs the language
to be used in the State Legislatures.
➤ Article 118 empowers each House of Parliament
to make rules for regulating its procedure and the con-
duct of its business.
➤ Article 343 declares the official language of the
Union to be Hindi in Devanagari script.
➤ The Official Languages Act was enacted by
Parliament in 1963 to provide for the continued use of
English alongside Hindi.

35.question_text_en:
The provision related to the admission or
establishment of new States is in:
35.question_text_hi:
The provision related to the admission or
establishment of new States is in:
35.explanation_en:
Article 2 of the Constitution of India empowers
Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new
States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 2 relates to the admission or establishment
of new states that were not previously part of the Indian
Union (e.g., Sikkim's admission via constitutional
amendment).
➤ In contrast, Article 3 empowers Parliament to form
new states or alter boundaries of existing States of
India.
➤ Article 1 declares that "India, that is Bharat, shall
be a Union of States".
➤ Article 4 stipulates that laws made under Article 2
or Article 3 are not considered constitutional amend-
ments under Article 368.
➤ These provisions are located within Part I of the
Indian Constitution, titled "The Union and its Territory".

36.question_text_en: Where does the Indus River rise from?
36.question_text_hi: Where does the Indus River rise from?

options.text_en: Peaks of the Nanda Devi hills
options.text_hi: Peaks of the Nanda Devi hills

36.explanation_en:
The Indus River originates in the northern slopes of
the Kailash range in southwestern Tibet, specifically
from a glacier near Bokhar Chu in the vicinity of Lake
Manasarovar.
Important Facts:
➤ In Tibet, the Indus River is traditionally known by the
name Singi Khamban (meaning 'Lion's Mouth').
➤ The river flows through Ladakh, entering India before
taking a sharp south-westerly bend around Nanga
Parbat into Pakistan.
➤ The total length of the Indus River is approximately
3,180 km, making it one of the longest rivers in Asia.
➤ Its major left-bank tributaries in India comprise the
'Panjnad': Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and
Sutlej.
➤ The sharing of its waters is governed by the Indus
Waters Treaty of 1960, brokered by the World
Bank.

North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

east of Chabahar in Pakistan.

39.question_text_en:
Which factor is responsible for maintaining Earth's
orbit around the Sun without the planet drifting away into
space?
39.question_text_hi:
Which factor is responsible for maintaining Earth's
orbit around the Sun without the planet drifting away into
space?
39.explanation_en:
The Sun's gravitational force exerts a continuous
centripetal pull on Earth, balancing its orbital velocity and
holding it in an elliptical orbit.
Important Facts:
➤ According to Newton's Universal Law of
Gravitation, gravitational attraction is directly propor-
tional to the product of masses and inversely propor-
tional to the square of the distance.
➤ Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of ap-
proximately 149.6 million kilometres (1
Astronomical Unit).
➤ The elliptical shape of planetary orbits is described by
Kepler's First Law of Planetary Motion.
➤ Earth travels along its orbit around the Sun with an
average orbital speed of about 29.78 km/s.
➤ Without gravitational force acting as a centripetal
force, Earth would fly off in a straight line tangentially
into space.

40.question_text_en:
Which phenomenon explains the bending of light as it
passes through Earth's atmosphere, affecting how
celestial objects appear?
40.question_text_hi:
Which phenomenon explains the bending of light as it
passes through Earth's atmosphere, affecting how
celestial objects appear?
40.explanation_en:
Atmospheric refraction is the bending of light rays
as they pass through atmospheric layers of varying opti-
cal density, making celestial objects appear slightly
higher than their true positions.
Important Facts:
➤ Atmospheric refraction causes the Sun to appear visi-
ble about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and 2
minutes after actual sunset.
➤ The apparent twinkling of stars at night is also
caused by continuous fluctuations in atmospheric refrac-
tion.
➤ Refraction occurs because the speed of light
changes when passing between media of different re-
fractive indices.
➤ Snell's Law quantitatively describes the relationship
between angles of incidence and refraction: n₁ sin θ₁ =
n₂ sin θ₂.
➤ Celestial objects near the horizon suffer the highest
degree of atmospheric refraction compared to those at
the zenith.

42.question_text_en:
Who is known for discovering the basic rules of
inheritance through experiments on pea plants?
42.question_text_hi:
Who is known for discovering the basic rules of
inheritance through experiments on pea plants?
42.explanation_en:
Gregor Johann Mendel discovered the fundamental
laws of inheritance through systematic hybridization ex-
periments on garden pea plants (*Pisum sativum*), earn-
ing him the title 'Father of Genetics'.
Important Facts:
➤ Mendel formulated the Law of Segregation, the
Law of Independent Assortment, and the Law
of Dominance.
➤ He conducted his pea plant experiments at St.
Thomas's Abbey in Brno between 1856 and 1863.
➤ Mendel published his groundbreaking work titled
*Experiments on Plant Hybridization* in 1866.
➤ His laws were independently rediscovered in 1900
by Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von
Tschermak.
➤ Charles Darwin authored *On the Origin of
Species* (1859), proposing the theory of evolution by
natural selection.

43.question_text_en:
What is the importance of using satellite technology
in monitoring climate change and environmental
degradation globally?
43.question_text_hi:
What is the importance of using satellite technology
in monitoring climate change and environmental
degradation globally?
43.explanation_en:
Earth observation satellites provide global observa-
tion, enabling continuous, wide-scale synoptic monitor-
ing of global climate variables, deforestation, and atmo-
spheric dynamics.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth observation satellites capture critical planetary
parameters such as sea-surface temperatures, ice-sheet
melt rates, and greenhouse gas concentrations.
➤ Remote sensing enables consistent monitoring of re-
mote regions like the polar ice caps and the deep
Amazon rainforest.
➤ India's ISRO operates dedicated remote sensing
constellations including the Cartosat, Resourcesat,
and Oceansat series.
➤ The Copernicus Programme operated by the
European Union is the world's largest earth observation
programme.
➤ Satellites operate in diverse orbits such as Low Earth
Orbit (LEO) for high-resolution imaging and
Geostationary Orbit (GEO) for meteorological tracking.

26.question_text_hi:

26.explanation_en:
Chapchar Kut is an agricultural festival celebrated in
Mizoram marking the completion of clearing bamboo
forests for jhum cultivation. Hornbill is held in
Nagaland, Losar is celebrated in Himalayan regions
(such as Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh), and
Pongal is celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
Important Facts:
➤ Chapchar Kut is celebrated during March after
clearing the jungle for shifting cultivation (jhum).
➤ The traditional bamboo dance Cheraw is a promi-
nent highlight of the Chapchar Kut festival.
➤ Hornbill Festival is celebrated annually from 1 to
10 December in Nagaland (Kisama heritage village).
➤ Losar marks the traditional Tibetan and Buddhist
New Year celebrated in Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal
Pradesh.
➤ Pongal is a multi-day harvest festival dedicated to
the Sun god, celebrated widely across Tamil Nadu.

27.question_text_en:
Which Sikh festival is celebrated annually in Muktsar
to honour the memory of the 'Chalis Mukte' (forty Sikh
martyrs) who died fighting against the Mughal emperor
Wazir Khan?
27.question_text_hi:
Which Sikh festival is celebrated annually in Muktsar
to honour the memory of the 'Chalis Mukte' (forty Sikh
martyrs) who died fighting against the Mughal emperor
Wazir Khan?
27.explanation_en:
The festival of Maghi (celebrated on the first day of the
Punjabi month of Magh) is held as Mela Maghi at
Muktsar Sahib to commemorate the bravery of the
Chalis Mukte (Forty Liberated Ones) who laid down
their lives in the Battle of Muktsar (1705).
Important Facts:
➤ The Battle of Khidrana (Muktsar) was fought in
1705 between the Mughal forces under Wazir Khan and
Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
➤ The forty Sikh soldiers who sacrificed their lives were
blessed by Guru Gobind Singh Ji as the Chalis Mukte
(Forty Liberated Ones).
➤ Following their sacrifice, the town of Khidrana was re-
named Sri Muktsar Sahib.
➤ Mai Bhago, a revered Sikh heroine, rallied and led
these forty warriors into the battlefield.
➤ The annual fair, Mela Maghi, is held on the day of
Makar Sankranti / Maghi at Sri Muktsar Sahib in Punjab.

28.question_text_en:
As of 2024, which BRICS country is the largest by
geographical area?
28.question_text_hi:
As of 2024, which BRICS country is the largest by
geographical area?
28.explanation_en:
Russia is the largest country in the world and among all
BRICS nations by total geographic landmass, spanning
an immense territory of over 17.1 million square
kilometres across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia.
Important Facts:
➤ Russia possesses a total surface area of approxi-
mately 17,098,242 sq km, making it the world's and
BRICS' largest nation by area.
➤ The five founding/early BRICS nations ranked by
land area are Russia, followed by China, Brazil,
India, and South Africa.
➤ The acronym BRIC was coined in 2001 by British
economist Jim O'Neill.
➤ South Africa officially joined the association in 2010,
transforming the bloc into BRICS.
➤ The BRICS group expanded at the beginning of 2024
to include new members like Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and
the UAE.

29.question_text_en: PM Jan Dhan Yojana primarily aims at:
29.question_text_hi: PM Jan Dhan Yojana primarily aims at:
29.explanation_en:
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a
national mission for comprehensive financial inclu-
sion, launched to ensure that every household across
India has access to basic banking services, savings ac-
counts, credit, remittance, and insurance.
Important Facts:
➤ PMJDY was launched by Prime Minister Narendra
Modi on 28 August 2014 with the slogan *"Mera
Khata, Bhagya Vidhata"*.
➤ The scheme provides basic savings bank deposit
(BSBD) zero-balance accounts to unbanked individuals.
➤ Beneficiaries receive a RuPay debit card with
built-in accidental insurance cover.
➤ An overdraft (OD) facility of up to Rs10,000 is
available to eligible account holders.
➤ PMJDY serves as the foundational pillar for the JAM
(Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) Trinity enabling di-
rect benefit transfers (DBT).

30.question_text_en:
The presence of a stepped water tank known as a
'surya-kund' with miniature temples carved on its steps is
a unique architectural feature of which temple style?
30.question_text_hi:
The presence of a stepped water tank known as a
'surya-kund' with miniature temples carved on its steps is
a unique architectural feature of which temple style?
30.explanation_en:
The stepped water tank called Surya-kund, lined with
numerous miniature shrines along its terraces and steps,
is the hallmark of the Solanki (Maru-Gurjara)
School of architecture, famously seen at the Sun
Temple in Modhera, Gujarat.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sun Temple at Modhera was built in 1026
CE during the reign of King Bhimdev I of the Solanki
dynasty.
➤ The temple complex consists of three main compo-
nents: the sanctum (Gudhamandapa), the assembly
hall (Sabhamandapa), and the stepped reservoir
(Surya-kund).
➤ The Surya-kund contains 108 miniature shrines
dedicated to various deities carved along the stepped
terraces.
➤ The Solanki school belongs to the western Indian
branch of the Nagara architectural order.
➤ The sanctum was designed so that the first rays of
the rising sun fell directly on the deity during equinoxes.

31.question_text_en:
Which three kingdoms emerged in the southern
regions of the Subcontinent around 400 BCE?
31.question_text_hi:
Which three kingdoms emerged in the southern
regions of the Subcontinent around 400 BCE?
31.explanation_en:
In ancient South India (Tamilakam), the three prominent
early ruling lineages known as the Muventhar (Three
Crowned Kings) were the Cholas, Cheras, and
Pandyas. They emerged during the late Megalithic /
early Sangam period.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sangam literature collectively refers to the
Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas as the Muventhar
(three crowned kings).
➤ The Cheras ruled over Kerala and western Tamil
Nadu, with their main port at Muziris and capital at
Vanji/Karur.
➤ The Cholas controlled the Kaveri delta and northern
Tamil Nadu, with their capital at Uraiyur and port at
Puhar (Kaveripattinam).
➤ The Pandyas ruled over southern Tamil Nadu, with
their ancient capital at Madurai and port at Korkai.
➤ Ashoka's Major Rock Edict II (3rd century BCE) men-
tions the Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, and
Keralaputras as border states in the south.

32.question_text_en:
Which of the following was first introduced under the
Act of 1892?
32.question_text_hi:
Which of the following was first introduced under the
Act of 1892?
32.explanation_en:
The Indian Councils Act 1892 enlarged the legisla-
tive councils and gave members the power to discuss
the annual financial statement (budget) and ask
questions on domestic matters. Direct elections were in-
troduced in 1919, while bicameralism at the Centre
came under the Government of India Act 1919.
Important Facts:
➤ Under the Indian Councils Act 1892, members
of the legislative councils were allowed to discuss the
budget, though they could not vote on it.
➤ Members were granted the right to address questions
to the executive on matters of public interest with prior
notice.
➤ The Act introduced an indirect system of
election/recommendation through bodies like universi-
ties, district boards, and municipalities.
➤ Direct elections and bicameralism at the central
level were introduced under the Government of
India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms).
➤ Provincial autonomy and responsible ministries in
provinces were established under the Government of
India Act 1935.

33.question_text_en:
Which of the following initiatives was explicitly
emphasised by Wood's Despatch of 1854?
33.question_text_hi:
Which of the following initiatives was explicitly
emphasised by Wood's Despatch of 1854?
33.explanation_en:
Wood's Despatch of 1854, referred to as the
'Magna Carta of English Education in India', placed
strong emphasis on female education, vernacular el-
ementary education, and secular schooling. It also rec-
ommended setting up universities in Calcutta, Bombay,
and Madras.
Important Facts:
➤ Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of
Control, sent this educational despatch to the Governor-
General Lord Dalhousie in 1854.
➤ It advocated secular education in government-aided
institutions and strongly supported the promotion of
female education.
➤ It recommended the establishment of Universities in
Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, which were es-
tablished in 1857.
➤ It introduced the Grants-in-Aid system to foster pri-
vate enterprise and voluntary efforts in education.

➤ It recommended vernacular languages as the
medium of instruction at primary levels and English for
higher education.

34.question_text_en: The objective of price control policies was:
34.question_text_hi: The objective of price control policies was:
34.explanation_en:
Price control policies (such as ceiling prices or ad-
ministered price mechanisms) are implemented by gov-
ernments primarily to stabilize the market, curb unrea-
sonable price spikes, and prevent inflation on essen-
tial goods and services.
Important Facts:
➤ A price ceiling sets a maximum legal price at
which a good or service can be sold to keep essentials
affordable for consumers.
➤ Government intervention through administered pric-
ing prevents hoarding, speculative price surges, and gal-
loping inflation.
➤ In India, the Essential Commodities Act, 1955
empowers authorities to regulate the supply, distribution,
and pricing of essential commodities.
➤ The Minimum Support Price (MSP) acts as a price
floor designed to protect farmers from sharp declines in
agricultural market prices.
➤ While price ceilings curb inflation, if set below equilib-
rium they can lead to excess demand and shortages in
the open market.

35.question_text_en:
The sector that benefited most from LPG
(Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) reforms is:
35.question_text_hi:
The sector that benefited most from LPG
(Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) reforms is:
35.explanation_en:
The New Economic Policy of 1991 (LPG reforms)
opened up trade and private investment, which mas-
sively propelled India's services sector—particularly
IT, telecommunications, banking, business processing,
and financial services—to become the leading driver of
GDP growth.
Important Facts:
➤ India introduced LPG reforms in 1991 under
Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance
Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
➤ The services sector (tertiary sector) registered
the highest sustained double-digit growth rates following
these structural reforms.
➤ Information Technology (IT) and Business Process
Management (BPM) emerged as the primary engines of
Indian software exports.
➤ Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows surged pre-
dominantly into service sub-sectors, including software,
telecommunications, and financial services.
➤ Today, the services sector contributes over 50% of
India's Gross Value Added (GVA).

36.question_text_en:
In which Articles of the Indian Constitution is the Right
to Equality given?
36.question_text_hi:
In which Articles of the Indian Constitution is the Right
to Equality given?
36.explanation_en:
The Right to Equality is enshrined in Articles 14
to 18 under Part III of the Constitution of India, guaran-
teeing equality before the law and prohibiting discrimina-
tion on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of
birth.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and
equal protection of the laws within India.
➤ Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds only
of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
➤ Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in mat-
ters of public employment.
➤ Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids
its practice in any form.
➤ Article 18 provides for the abolition of titles, except
military and academic distinctions.

to conduct legislative assembly elections in Jammu and
Kashmir.

special autonomous status to Jammu and Kashmir
within the Indian Union.

38.question_text_en:
The final authority to interpret the Constitution rests
with:
38.question_text_hi:
The final authority to interpret the Constitution rests
with:
38.explanation_en:
The Supreme Court of India is the ultimate
guardian, protector, and final interpreter of the
Constitution of India. Its interpretation of any consti-
tutional provision is binding on all courts and authorities
throughout the territory of India under Article 141.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 141 of the Constitution states that the law
declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all
courts within the territory of India.

➤ Article 132 and 133 provide appellate jurisdiction
to the Supreme Court in constitutional cases involving
substantial questions of law.
➤ The Supreme Court has the power of Judicial
Review to strike down any legislative enactment or ex-
ecutive action violating the Constitution.
➤ In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case
(1973), the Supreme Court enunciated the Basic
Structure doctrine, limiting Parliament's amending
powers.
➤ The Supreme Court of India was established on 26
January 1950, succeeding the Federal Court of India.

39.question_text_en:
Which factor is responsible for the apparent shift of
constellations visible in the night sky over different
seasons of the year?
39.question_text_hi:
Which factor is responsible for the apparent shift of
constellations visible in the night sky over different
seasons of the year?
39.explanation_en:
As the Earth undergoes revolution around the Sun
along its orbit, the night side of the Earth faces in differ-
ent directions in space over the course of a year.
Consequently, different constellations appear visible dur-
ing different seasons.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth's revolution takes approximately 365.25
days to complete one orbit around the Sun.
➤ The daily rising and setting of stars across the sky
from east to west is caused by Earth's rotation on its
axis.
➤ The seasonal variation of constellations visible at
midnight occurs because the Earth's night face looks out
toward different celestial coordinates as it revolves.
➤ Constellations visible only at particular times of the
year are termed seasonal constellations (e.g.,
Orion in winter, Scorpius in summer).
➤ Constellations located close to celestial poles that re-
main visible year-round from high latitudes are known as
circumpolar constellations.

40.question_text_en: Avalanches are most likely to occur when?
40.question_text_hi: Avalanches are most likely to occur when?

options.text_en: The snow begins to melt rapidly on slopes
options.text_hi: The snow begins to melt rapidly on slopes

options.text_en: The glaciers slowly move downhill over time
options.text_hi: The glaciers slowly move downhill over time

options.text_en: The rivers overflow due to seasonal rainfall
options.text_hi: The rivers overflow due to seasonal rainfall

options.text_en: The rocks erode gradually along riverbanks
options.text_hi: The rocks erode gradually along riverbanks

40.explanation_en:
An avalanche occurs when a mass of snow, ice, and
debris suddenly detaches and slides rapidly down a
mountain slope. Rapid warming or melting weakens the
structural bond between snow layers and lubricates the
surface underneath, triggering sudden slides.
Important Facts:
➤ Avalanches are rapid downward movements of
snowpacks triggered on steep slopes, generally between
30° and 45°.
➤ Sudden rises in temperature or rapid snowmelt
destabilize the cohesive forces within the snowpack.
➤ The presence of weak structural layers, such as hoar-
frost or loose granular snow beneath fresh heavy snow,
increases avalanche risk.
➤ High wind speeds and seismic tremors are other nat-
ural factors contributing to avalanche initiation.
➤ In India, snow avalanches frequently occur in high-al-
titude Himalayan regions of Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh,
Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand.

41.question_text_en:
Which state/UT is home to the 'Jarawa' and
'Sentinelese' tribal groups?
41.question_text_hi:
Which state/UT is home to the 'Jarawa' and
'Sentinelese' tribal groups?
41.explanation_en:
The Jarawa and Sentinelese are indigenous hunter-
gatherer communities residing in the Andaman and
Nicobar Islands. They are classified as Particularly
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) of Negrito heritage.
Important Facts:
➤ The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home
to six indigenous tribes: Great Andamanese, Onge,
Jarawa, Sentinelese, Shompen, and Nicobarese.
➤ The Sentinelese inhabit North Sentinel Island and
remain largely isolated from modern civilization.
➤ The Jarawa inhabit parts of South Andaman and
Middle Andaman islands.
➤ Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, and
Shompen are officially recognized as Particularly
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
➤ The Ministry of Tribal Affairs recognizes 75 PVTGs
across 18 states and the Union Territory of Andaman
and Nicobar Islands.

42.question_text_en:
Any land left uncultivated for a period of more than
five years is classified as:
42.question_text_hi:
Any land left uncultivated for a period of more than
five years is classified as:
42.explanation_en:
According to land-use classification in India, land that is
available for cultivation but has been left uncultivated for
more than five successive years is termed as
Culturable Wasteland. It can be brought under culti-
vation through reclamation efforts.
Important Facts:
➤ Current Fallow represents land that is left unculti-
vated for one agricultural year or less.
➤ Fallow other than current fallow refers to
cropland left uncultivated for between one and five
years.
➤ Culturable Wasteland includes land lying fallow
for more than five consecutive years, which can
be cultivated after reclamation.
➤ Barren and Unculturable Land includes land
that cannot be cultivated with available technology (e.g.,
steep mountains, deserts, rocky outcrops).
➤ Land use statistics in India are systematically com-
piled by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics un-
der nine standard categories.

43.question_text_en:
The gradual reduction of water flow from 18-20 litres
to 20-80 drops per minute mainly indicates:
43.question_text_hi:
The gradual reduction of water flow from 18-20 litres
to 20-80 drops per minute mainly indicates:

options.text_en: Deliberate regulation for efficient irrigation of plants
options.text_hi: Deliberate regulation for efficient irrigation of plants

options.text_en: Leakage due to weak bamboo joints
options.text_hi: Leakage due to weak bamboo joints

43.explanation_en:
In traditional bamboo drip irrigation systems
(practiced widely in Meghalaya), hillside stream water
(18–20 litres/min) is diverted through bamboo pipes and
regulated step-by-step so that it trickles at 20–80
drops per minute directly at the roots of plants for
water efficiency.
Important Facts:
➤ The bamboo drip irrigation system is an in-
digenous traditional water harvesting technique exten-
sively practiced in Meghalaya.
➤ In this method, 18–20 litres of water entering the
bamboo channel system per minute is gradually reduced
to 20–80 drops per minute at the plant site.
➤ It is ideally used to irrigate black pepper and betel
leaf plantations along steep, terraced hill slopes.
➤ The system channels spring water across hundreds
of metres using interconnected, perforated bamboo
pipes without using pumps.
➤ The reduction in discharge is intentionally regulated
through pipe diameters and slope positioning to prevent
soil erosion and water wastage.

44.question_text_en:
If India fails to provide education and employment to
its growing working-age population, what will happen to
the demographic dividend?
44.question_text_hi:
If India fails to provide education and employment to
its growing working-age population, what will happen to
the demographic dividend?

options.text_en: It will convert into a demographic burden.
options.text_hi: It will convert into a demographic burden.

options.text_en: It will reduce the dependency ratio further.
options.text_hi: It will reduce the dependency ratio further.

44.explanation_en:
A demographic dividend yields economic prosperity only
when the working-age population is educated, skilled,
and gainfully employed. Without adequate schooling,
health, and jobs, high numbers of unemployed youth
turn the potential dividend into a demographic bur-
den / disaster.
Important Facts:
➤ The demographic dividend refers to the eco-
nomic growth potential resulting from shifts in a
population’s age structure, specifically when the work-
ing-age share is larger.
➤ The working-age population is universally defined as
individuals aged 15 to 64 years (or 15–59 years).
➤ The dependency ratio measures the proportion of
dependents (children and elderly) relative to the working-
age population.
➤ Failure to generate productive jobs leads to youth un-
deremployment, social instability, and increased fiscal
pressure on public finances.
➤ India's demographic window of opportunity opened
around 2005-06 and is projected to last until roughly the
mid-2050s.

45.question_text_en:
Which species was the focus of the first complete
mitochondrial genome analysis in India?
45.question_text_hi:
Which species was the focus of the first complete
mitochondrial genome analysis in India?
45.explanation_en:
Researchers in India successfully sequenced and ana-
lyzed the complete mitochondrial genome (mi-
togenome) of the Madras Hedgehog
(*Paraechinus nudiventris*), uncovering key evolutionary
divergence details and genetic insights for this lesser-
known insectivorous mammal.
Important Facts:

➤ The Madras Hedgehog (*Paraechinus nudiven-
tris*) is a small nocturnal mammal native to the dry
scrublands and grasslands of southern India.
➤ The circular mitochondrial genome of the Madras
Hedgehog was assembled to a length of approximately
17,232 base pairs.
➤ The study identified 13 protein-coding genes, 22
transfer RNAs (tRNAs), and two ribosomal RNAs
(rRNAs) characteristic of vertebrate mitogenomes.
➤ The Madras Hedgehog curls into a spiny ball as a pri-
mary natural defense mechanism against predators.
➤ The species is listed under Schedule II of the Wildlife
(Protection) Act, 1972 in India.

46.question_text_en:
Which taxonomic category is used for plants instead
of 'Phylum' used for animals?
46.question_text_hi:
Which taxonomic category is used for plants instead
of 'Phylum' used for animals?
46.explanation_en:
In biological classification, while animals are grouped
into different Phyla (singular: Phylum) below the
Kingdom level, plants and fungi are historically orga-
nized into equivalent taxonomic categories known as
Divisions.
Important Facts:
➤ The hierarchical taxonomic levels from highest to low-
est are: Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class →
Order → Family → Genus → Species.
➤ The International Code of Nomenclature for algae,
fungi, and plants (ICN) permits the use of Division syn-
onymously with Phylum.
➤ Plant division names typically end with the standard
suffix -phyta (e.g., Bryophyta, Pteridophyta,
Magnoliophyta).
➤ Carl Linnaeus laid the foundation of modern bio-
logical taxonomy and the binomial nomenclature system
in his work *Systema Naturae*.
➤ Species is the basic and lowest fundamental unit of
biological classification.

47.question_text_en:
Which nutrient is primarily responsible for muscle
repair?
47.question_text_hi:
Which nutrient is primarily responsible for muscle
repair?
47.explanation_en:
Proteins are the body's building blocks, composed of
amino acids required for the synthesis of cellular struc-
tures, tissue growth, and the repair of damaged
muscles.
Important Facts:
➤ Proteins are polymers made up of amino acids
linked together by peptide bonds.
➤ Nine out of twenty amino acids are considered es-
sential amino acids because the human body can-
not synthesize them internally.
➤ Structural proteins such as actin and myosin form
the contractile components of muscle fibres.
➤ Severe protein deficiency in infants and children
causes deficiency diseases such as Kwashiorkor and
Marasmus.
➤ Dietary sources rich in proteins include pulses, eggs,
milk, fish, soybeans, and lean meats.

➤ The initiative aims to converge schemes across agri-
culture and allied sectors to augment farm income and
local storage.
➤ Progress across the 100 districts is tracked through a
dedicated monitoring framework on the lines of the
Aspirational Districts Programme.

to prevent floods in Hyderabad.

lowing which modern Hyderabad's urban flood drainage
system was planned under Sir M. Visvesvaraya.

Among four colleagues, the total monthly savings is
Rs40,000. X and Y together save as much as Z and W. X
saves Rs2,000 more than Z. W saves three times as much
as Z. Who saves the least amount?
13.explanation_en:
Right option (C): Z
Explanation
Total monthly savings: X + Y + Z + W = Rs40,000.
Since X + Y = Z + W, each pair saves Rs20,000.
Given W = 3Z:
Z + 3Z = 20,000 ⇒ 4Z = 20,000 ⇒ Z = Rs5,000, and W =
Rs15,000.
Also, X = Z + 2,000 = Rs7,000, so Y = 20,000 − 7,000 =
Rs13,000.
Comparing all four (X = Rs7,000, Y = Rs13,000, Z =
Rs5,000, W = Rs15,000), Z saves the least amount.
✔ Answer: (C)

16.explanation_en:

Explanation
The operation a ★ b follows the rule (a × b) + (a + b):
• 3 ★ 5 = (3 × 5) + (3 + 5) = 15 + 8 = 23.
• 4 ★ 6 = (4 × 6) + (4 + 6) = 24 + 10 = 34.

✔ Answer: (C)

birthright and I shall have it."

"Father of Indian Unrest".

32.question_text_en:
Which Articles of the Indian Constitution are related
to the "Right to Freedom"?
32.question_text_hi:
Which Articles of the Indian Constitution are related
to the "Right to Freedom"?
32.explanation_en:
The Right to Freedom is guaranteed under Articles
19 to 22 in Part III of the Constitution of India, covering
basic civil liberties, protection against arbitrary arrest,
and the fundamental right to life.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 19 guarantees six democratic free-
doms (speech, assembly, association, movement, resi-
dence, and profession).
➤ Article 20 provides protection in respect of convic-
tion for offences (against ex-post-facto law, double jeop-
ardy, and self-incrimination).
➤ Article 21 guarantees the Protection of Life
and Personal Liberty.
➤ Article 21A makes free and compulsory education
for children aged 6 to 14 a Fundamental Right (added by
the 86th Amendment Act, 2002).
➤ Article 22 provides protection against arrest and
detention in certain cases.

The constitutional amendment which added
Fundamental Duties to the Constitution was:
33.question_text_hi:
The constitutional amendment which added
Fundamental Duties to the Constitution was:
33.explanation_en:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
inserted Part IVA and Article 51A into the Indian
Constitution, adding 10 Fundamental Duties based
on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh
Committee.
Important Facts:
➤ The concept of Fundamental Duties was borrowed
from the constitution of the former USSR.
➤ Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added in
1976.
➤ The 11th Fundamental Duty (providing educa-
tion to children aged 6 to 14) was added by the 86th
Amendment Act, 2002.
➤ Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and can-
not be enforced directly through writ petitions.
➤ The 42nd Amendment is commonly referred to as the
"Mini-Constitution" due to its sweeping structural
changes.

________ to the Supreme Court.

________ to the Supreme Court.

judgment, decree, or final order of a High Court in civil
proceedings, provided the High Court certifies it involves
a substantial question of law of general importance.
Important Facts:

Supreme Court in constitutional cases.
➤ Article 133 specifically deals with the appellate ju-
risdiction of the Supreme Court in civil matters.

Supreme Court in criminal matters.
➤ Article 136 provides for Special Leave to
Appeal (SLP) granted at the discretion of the Supreme
Court.

on 28 January 1950.

implementation of the Sixth Schedule.

nize autonomous districts.

legislative powers into Union, State, and Concurrent

36.question_text_en:
What is the correct scientific explanation for the
occurrence of solar and lunar eclipses based on the
alignment of celestial bodies?
36.question_text_hi:
What is the correct scientific explanation for the
occurrence of solar and lunar eclipses based on the
alignment of celestial bodies?
36.explanation_en:
Eclipses occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon
align in a straight line (known as syzygy). A solar
eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the
Sun and Earth, while a lunar eclipse occurs when the
Earth comes between the Sun and Moon, casting shad-
ows.
Important Facts:
➤ The straight-line configuration of three celestial bod-
ies in a gravitational system is termed syzygy.
➤ A solar eclipse occurs on a New Moon day
(Amavasya).
➤ A lunar eclipse occurs on a Full Moon night
(Purnima).
➤ The darker central part of the shadow during an
eclipse is called the umbra, and the lighter outer part is
the penumbra.
➤ Eclipses do not occur every month because the
Moon's orbit is tilted by about 5 degrees relative to
Earth's orbital plane.

37.question_text_en:
Which movement of the Earth is responsible for the
occurrence of one complete year and influences seasonal
cycles globally?
37.question_text_hi:
Which movement of the Earth is responsible for the
occurrence of one complete year and influences seasonal
cycles globally?
37.explanation_en:
The revolution of the Earth around the Sun in
an elliptical orbit takes approximately 365.25 days,
defining one calendar year. Along with the Earth's tilted
axis of 23.5 degrees, revolution is directly responsible for
the cycle of seasons.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth takes 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes,
and 46 seconds to complete one revolution.
➤ The rotation of the Earth on its axis causes day and
night and takes approximately 24 hours.
➤ Earth's axis of rotation is tilted at an angle of 66.5
degrees to its orbital plane (or 23.5 degrees from
the perpendicular).
➤ Perihelion is the point when Earth is closest to the
Sun (around January 3).
➤ Aphelion is the point when Earth is farthest from
the Sun (around July 4).

38.question_text_en:
What is the main type of rock found in the Deccan
Trap region?
38.question_text_hi:
What is the main type of rock found in the Deccan
Trap region?
38.explanation_en:
The Deccan Trap is composed predominantly of
basaltic igneous rocks formed by volcanic fissure
eruptions during the late Cretaceous period. Weathering
of these igneous rocks led to the formation of fertile
black cotton soil (Regur).
Important Facts:
➤ The Deccan volcanic province was formed around
65–66 million years ago.
➤ Basalt is an extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock rich in
iron and magnesium.
➤ The Deccan Trap covers major parts of
Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
➤ Weathering of Deccan basalt generates black soil,
exceptionally suited for cotton cultivation.
➤ The step-like landscape feature of horizontal lava
flows gives it the Scandinavian name "Trap", meaning
stairs.

39.question_text_en:
In the study of human settlements, what type of rural
settlement is characterized by a "dispersed" pattern?
39.question_text_hi:
In the study of human settlements, what type of rural
settlement is characterized by a "dispersed" pattern?
39.explanation_en:
A dispersed settlement pattern (also known as
isolated settlement) consists of isolated huts or scat-
tered hamlets located far apart across hills, valleys, or
agricultural fields rather than clustered together.
Important Facts:
➤ Dispersed settlements are commonly found in rugged
terrains like the Himalayas, Meghalaya, and parts of
Kerala.
➤ Nucleated or clustered settlements are char-
acterized by houses built closely together, common in
fertile alluvial plains.
➤ Linear settlements develop along physical or
transport corridors such as roads, railway lines, rivers, or
canals.
➤ Fragmented terrain and abundant agricultural land re-
quirements encourage the dispersion of dwellings.
➤ Semi-clustered settlements result from the
segregation or fragmentation of a large compact village.

heat-resistant sheets along its basal cleavage planes.

41.question_text_en:
The process of breakdown of glucose into pyruvate
occurs in which part of the cell?
41.question_text_hi:
The process of breakdown of glucose into pyruvate
occurs in which part of the cell?
41.explanation_en:
The breakdown of glucose into pyruvate occurs during
glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm of
the cell. This metabolic pathway does not require oxygen
and produces a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH mole-
cules.
Important Facts:
➤ Glycolysis is also known as the EMP pathway
(Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas pathway).
➤ In glycolysis, one 6-carbon molecule of glucose is
converted into two 3-carbon molecules of pyruvate.
➤ The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) and oxida-
tive phosphorylation take place inside the mitochon-
dria.
➤ Glycolysis is a universal pathway occurring in both
aerobic and anaerobic organisms.
➤ Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses
of the cell" because the majority of ATP synthesis oc-
curs there.

42.question_text_en:
Which scientific technology allows farmers and
scientists to monitor crop conditions, soil moisture and
agricultural patterns using satellite data?
42.question_text_hi:
Which scientific technology allows farmers and
scientists to monitor crop conditions, soil moisture and
agricultural patterns using satellite data?
42.explanation_en:
Remote sensing technology captures electromag-
netic radiation reflected or emitted from the Earth's sur-
face via satellite and airborne sensors, enabling preci-
sion assessment of crop health, vegetative indices, and
soil moisture levels.
Important Facts:
➤ The Normalized Difference Vegetation
Index (NDVI) is a standard remote sensing index used
to measure plant health.
➤ India's dedicated remote sensing satellite series is
known as the IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) satel-
lite system.
➤ The National Remote Sensing Centre
(NRSC) is situated at Hyderabad under ISRO.
➤ Remote sensing is broadly classified into active re-
mote sensing (uses own energy source like Radar)
and passive remote sensing (uses Sun's reflected
light).
➤ The Government of India utilizes the FASAL project
(Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-mete-
orology and Land-based observations) for crop
forecasting.

43.question_text_en:
The Sirkeer Malkoha, a rare bird species recently
reported in the news, is typically found in the plains of
which state?
43.question_text_hi:
The Sirkeer Malkoha, a rare bird species recently
reported in the news, is typically found in the plains of
which state?
43.explanation_en:
The Sirkeer Malkoha (*Taccocua leschenaultii*), a
non-parasitic species of cuckoo, was sighted and re-
ported in the grassland and scrub plains of
Uttarakhand (particularly the Terai-Bhabar and foothill
belts), drawing birdwatchers' attention.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sirkeer Malkoha belongs to the cuckoo family
Cuculidae.
➤ Unlike many other cuckoos, it is non-parasitic and
builds its own nests to rear chicks.
➤ Its scientific name is *Taccocua leschenaultii*,
named after French botanist Jean-Baptiste Leschenault.
➤ It thrives predominantly in dry scrub, open thorny
forests, and dry deciduous biomes.
➤ The bird is distinguished by its heavy, curved, red-
and-yellow hooked bill and long graduated tail.

13.question_text_hi:
A traveler reaches an oasis with a full canteen of
water. Every day he crosses a desert dune, he drinks one-
third of the water remaining in his canteen plus 1 liter
more. After 2 days, his canteen is empty. How much water
did he start with?
13.explanation_en:
Right option (B): 3.75 liters
Explanation
Let the initial amount of water be x liters.
• After Day 1, water left = (2/3)x − 1.
• After Day 2, water left = (2/3)((2/3)x − 1) − 1 = 0.
⇒ (2/3)x − 1 = 1.5 ⇒ (2/3)x = 2.5 ⇒ x = 2.5 × 3 / 2 = 3.75
liters.
✔ Answer: (B)

together. Box C weighs 10 kg more than Box D. Box B
weighs one-third of Box A. Which box is the heaviest?

Explanation
Total weight: A + B + C + D = 120 kg.
Since A + B = C + D, each pair weighs 60 kg.
• Given B = (1/3)A ⇒ A + (1/3)A = 60 ⇒ (4/3)A = 60 ⇒ A
= 45 kg, and B = 15 kg.
• Given C − D = 10 and C + D = 60 ⇒ C = 35 kg, and D
= 25 kg.
Comparing all four (A = 45 kg, B = 15 kg, C = 35 kg, D =
25 kg), Box A is the heaviest.

In Athletics, specifically in the 100 m sprint, what is
the maximum allowable "Tailwind" for a performance to be
officially recognized as a record?
26.explanation_en:
According to World Athletics technical rules, the
maximum allowable tailwind for record validation in out-
door sprint events (up to 200 m) and horizontal jumps is
+2.0 metres per second (+2.0 m/s). Any wind as-
sistance above this threshold invalidates record status.
Important Facts:
➤ The +2.0 m/s wind limit applies to the 100 m, 200
m, 100 m/110 m hurdles, long jump, and triple
jump.
➤ Wind velocity is measured using an electronic instru-
ment called a wind gauge (anemometer).
➤ For the 100 m sprint, wind assistance is measured for
a duration of 10 seconds, starting from the flash of the
starter's gun.
➤ Performances with wind exceeding +2.0 m/s are
marked as wind-assisted (w) and cannot count for
world, area, or national records.
➤ World Athletics is the international governing
body for the sport of athletics, headquartered in Monaco.

27.question_text_hi:
The festival of 'Sarhul' is a major New Year
celebration that involves the ritualistic worship of the Sal
tree. This nature-centric festival is primarily observed by
the Munda oraon and Ho tribes in which Indian state?
27.explanation_en:
Sarhul is the most prominent spring festival celebrated
in Jharkhand by tribal communities such as the
Oraon, Munda, and Ho. It marks the tribal New Year
and worships nature through the blooming of the Sal
tree (Shorea robusta).
Important Facts:
➤ Sarhul is celebrated in the Hindu month of Chaitra
on the third day of Shukla Paksha.
➤ The festival commemorates the marriage of Mother
Earth with the Sun, heralding the arrival of spring.
➤ The village priest, known as the Pahan, conducts
traditional rituals and distributes Sal flowers as
prasad.
➤ Traditional dances and music accompanied by instru-
ments like Mandar and Dhol form an essential part of
the celebrations.
➤ No agricultural activities like sowing begin until Sarhul
rituals are performed.

30.explanation_en:
Abhigyan Shakuntalam is a masterpiece Sanskrit
play authored by the classical playwright and poet
Kalidasa. The play dramatises the love story of King
Dushyanta and Shakuntala, adapted from the epic
Mahabharata.
Important Facts:
➤ Kalidasa lived during the Gupta period and is re-
garded as the greatest poet-dramatist of classical
Sanskrit.
➤ His other major plays include Malavikagnimitram
and Vikramorvashiyam.
➤ Kalidasa's celebrated epic poems (Mahakavya) are
Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.
➤ His famous lyrical poems (Khandakavya) are
Meghaduta and Ritusamhara.
➤ *Abhigyan Shakuntalam* was among the earliest
Indian literary works translated into Western languages,
translated by Sir William Jones in 1789.

multilateral trade agreements?

options.text_en: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
options.text_hi: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

32.explanation_en:
The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
(GATT) governed international multilateral trade rules
from 1948 until it was officially superseded by the World
Trade Organization (WTO) on 1 January 1995
following the Marrakesh Agreement.
Important Facts:
➤ GATT was signed by 23 nations in Geneva in 1947
and came into effect on 1 January 1948.

➤ The WTO was born out of the Uruguay Round of
trade negotiations, which spanned from 1986 to 1994.
➤ Unlike GATT, which was an ad-hoc legal agreement
with no institutional foundation, the WTO is a full-fledged
permanent international organisation.
➤ The WTO encompasses trade in goods (GATT),
trade in services (GATS), and intellectual prop-
erty rights (TRIPS).
➤ The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is
situated in Geneva, Switzerland.

33.question_text_en:
Which element is essential in a "Panchayatana"
temple layout?
33.question_text_hi:
Which element is essential in a "Panchayatana"
temple layout?
33.explanation_en:
A Panchayatana temple style consists of a main
central shrine surrounded by four subsidiary
shrines, making a total of five shrines. The term
originates from the Sanskrit words 'Pancha' (five) and
'Ayatana' (shrine/abode).
Important Facts:
➤ The Panchayatana layout is a prominent feature
of ancient and medieval Nagara and Dravida archi-

tecture.
➤ Famous examples include the Kandariya
Mahadeva Temple and Lakshmana Temple at
Khajuraho.
➤ In Odisha, the Brahmeshwara Temple in
Bhubaneswar is built on the Panchayatana plan.
➤ The subsidiary shrines are typically placed at the four
corners of a raised rectangular plinth (jagati).
➤ The layout symbolises a central presiding deity
flanked by four complementary secondary deities.

34.question_text_en:

34.question_text_hi:
The model that was adopted for India's Second Five-
Year Plan was:
34.explanation_en:
India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961) was
based on the Mahalanobis Model, formulated by
renowned statistician Prasanta Chandra
Mahalanobis, which emphasised heavy industrialisa-
tion and the development of basic capital goods indus-
tries.
Important Facts:
➤ The First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956) was based on
the Harrod-Domar Model focusing primarily on agri-
culture.
➤ The Second Plan laid the groundwork for public-sec-
tor steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur.
➤ P.C. Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical
Institute (ISI) in Kolkata in 1931.
➤ National Statistics Day is celebrated every year in
India on 29 June to mark the birth anniversary of P.C.
Mahalanobis.
➤ The Second Plan aimed at a rapid 25% increase in
national income through rapid industrialisation.

35.question_text_en:
Fill in the blank: Article ____ explicitly states that
courts cannot question the validity of Parliamentary
proceedings.
35.question_text_hi:
Fill in the blank: Article ____ explicitly states that
courts cannot question the validity of Parliamentary
proceedings.
35.explanation_en:
Article 122 of the Constitution of India provides immu-
nity to parliamentary proceedings, stating that the validity
of any proceedings in Parliament cannot be called in
question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of pro-
cedure.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 122(1) prohibits courts from inquiring into
parliamentary proceedings on grounds of irregularity of
procedure.
➤ Article 122(2) shields officers and members of
Parliament from court jurisdiction regarding powers exer-
cised for regulating procedure or conducting business.
➤ Article 120 deals with the language to be used
in Parliament (Hindi or English).
➤ Article 121 restricts discussions in Parliament re-
garding the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court or
High Courts.
➤ Article 123 empowers the President to pro-
mulgate Ordinances during the recess of
Parliament.

36.question_text_en:
The schedule which deals with anti-defection
provisions is:
36.question_text_hi:
The schedule which deals with anti-defection
provisions is:
36.explanation_en:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution con-
tains the anti-defection law, which lays down the
provisions regarding the disqualification of members of
Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defec-
tion.
Important Facts:

➤ The Tenth Schedule was added to the Constitution by
the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
➤ The law was enacted during the prime ministership of
Rajiv Gandhi to curb political opportunism.
➤ The question of disqualification under the Tenth
Schedule is decided by the Chairman or Speaker of
the respective House.
➤ The Supreme Court ruled in the landmark Kihoto
Hollohan case (1992) that the Speaker's decision is
subject to judicial review.
➤ The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act,
2003 omitted the provision protecting one-third splits
and limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of
the lower house.
